---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m1p0t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumBanks, AdminBanks

Banks == 1 .. NumBanks
NoOne == 0

VARIABLES token, state, engine, adminGrant, settled
vars == <<token, state, engine, adminGrant, settled>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Banks
  /\ state \in [Banks -> {"idle", "waiting", "posting"}]
  /\ engine \in Banks \cup {NoOne}
  /\ adminGrant \in Banks \cup {NoOne}
  /\ settled \in [Banks -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ token = 1
  /\ state = [b \in Banks |-> "idle"]
  /\ engine = NoOne
  /\ adminGrant = NoOne
  /\ settled = [b \in Banks |-> FALSE]

QueueBatch(b) ==
  /\ state[b] = "idle"
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![b] = "waiting"]
  /\ settled' = [settled EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, engine, adminGrant>>

\* The token slides forward only while the engine is idle and the bank it is
\* parked on has nothing queued, so it never abandons a waiting member.
AdvanceToken ==
  /\ engine = NoOne
  /\ state[token] # "waiting"
  /\ token' = (token % NumBanks) + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<state, engine, adminGrant, settled>>

SeizeByToken(b) ==
  /\ state[b] = "waiting"
  /\ token = b
  /\ engine = NoOne
  /\ engine' = b
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![b] = "posting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, adminGrant, settled>>

IssueOverride(b) ==
  /\ b \in AdminBanks
  /\ adminGrant = NoOne
  /\ adminGrant' = b
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, state, engine, settled>>

\* The supervisor's override lets an approved bank skip the ring order, but
\* it still may not barge in on a batch that is already being posted.
SeizeByOverride(b) ==
  /\ adminGrant = b
  /\ state[b] = "waiting"
  /\ engine = NoOne
  /\ engine' = b
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![b] = "posting"]
  /\ adminGrant' = NoOne
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, settled>>

ReleaseEngine(b) ==
  /\ state[b] = "posting"
  /\ engine = b
  /\ engine' = NoOne
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
  /\ settled' = [settled EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, adminGrant>>

SeizeAny == \E b \in Banks : SeizeByToken(b)
ReleaseAny == \E b \in Banks : ReleaseEngine(b)

Next ==
  \/ AdvanceToken
  \/ SeizeAny
  \/ ReleaseAny
  \/ \E b \in Banks : QueueBatch(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : IssueOverride(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : SeizeByOverride(b)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(AdvanceToken)
  /\ SF_vars(SeizeAny)
  /\ WF_vars(ReleaseAny)

\* The substantive claim: the engine's owner field and the banks' phases stay
\* coherent, which is exactly what makes the engine single-occupancy.
EngineOwnershipCoherent ==
  /\ \A b \in Banks : state[b] = "posting" => engine = b
  /\ engine # NoOne => state[engine] = "posting"

\* Progress guaranteed by the circulating token plus release fairness.
EveryQueuedBatchSettles ==
  \A b \in Banks : (state[b] = "waiting") ~> (settled[b] = TRUE)
=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    NumBanks = 3
    AdminBanks = {1}

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT EngineOwnershipCoherent

PROPERTY EveryQueuedBatchSettles
nl:
A national clearing house runs the nightly interbank settlement batch. Several member banks each hold a batch of payment instructions that must be pushed through a single shared posting engine, and the engine can only work one bank's batch at a time. Access to the engine is arbitrated by a settlement token that circulates around a ring of the member banks in a fixed order. The token moves one position around the ring at a time, and the clearing house only lets the token move while the posting engine is standing idle and while the bank the token is parked on has nothing queued, so the token never slides away underneath a batch that is mid-post and never abandons a member that is still waiting for its turn.

A bank that has instructions to clear first queues its batch, which puts it in the waiting phase and clears any earlier settled mark it carried. A waiting bank may seize the posting engine only when the settlement token is currently parked on it and the engine is free; at that moment the engine records that bank as its owner and the bank moves into the posting phase. When the bank has pushed its batch through, it releases the engine, returns to idle, and its batch is marked settled.

The clearing house supervisor also has a privileged admin override. The supervisor may issue an override grant to one of the banks on the approved override list, provided no override grant is already outstanding. A bank holding an outstanding override grant may seize the posting engine without waiting for the token to reach it, but the override still does not let it barge in on a batch that is already being posted: the engine must be free. Taking the engine on an override consumes the grant.

The full action set is: queue a batch at an idle bank, advance the settlement token one position around the ring while the engine is idle and the parked bank has nothing queued, seize the engine as the token-holding waiting bank, issue an admin override grant to an approved bank, seize the engine using an outstanding override grant, and release the engine when the batch has been posted.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The posting engine's owner field and the banks' own phases never disagree, so a bank is in the posting phase only when the engine names that bank as its owner and a named owner is always genuinely posting, which means two banks can never be pushing batches through the engine at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bank that queues a batch eventually has that batch marked settled.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m8p2t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumBlocks, SplitAt, FleetSize, MinBerth, MaxBerth

Blocks == 1 .. NumBlocks
Areas == {"north", "south"}
NoArea == "none"
NoBlock == 0

AreaOf(b) == IF b <= SplitAt THEN "north" ELSE "south"

VARIABLES parked, berth, areaAuth, blockAuth, shuttle
vars == <<parked, berth, areaAuth, blockAuth, shuttle>>

RECURSIVE ParkedUpTo(_)
ParkedUpTo(k) == IF k = 0 THEN 0 ELSE parked[k] + ParkedUpTo(k - 1)

OnTrack == ParkedUpTo(NumBlocks)

TypeOK ==
  /\ parked \in [Blocks -> 0 .. FleetSize]
  /\ berth \in [Blocks -> MinBerth .. MaxBerth]
  /\ areaAuth \in Areas \cup {NoArea}
  /\ blockAuth \in Blocks \cup {NoBlock}
  /\ shuttle \in 0 .. FleetSize

Init ==
  /\ parked = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b = 1 THEN FleetSize ELSE 0]
  /\ berth = [b \in Blocks |-> MaxBerth]
  /\ areaAuth = NoArea
  /\ blockAuth = NoBlock
  /\ shuttle = 0

\* Layered authority: the area-level grant must be in hand before any
\* block-level grant inside that area can be taken.
TakeArea(a) ==
  /\ areaAuth = NoArea
  /\ areaAuth' = a
  /\ UNCHANGED <<parked, berth, blockAuth, shuttle>>

TakeBlock(b) ==
  /\ areaAuth = AreaOf(b)
  /\ blockAuth = NoBlock
  /\ blockAuth' = b
  /\ UNCHANGED <<parked, berth, areaAuth, shuttle>>

LiftOnto(b, k) ==
  /\ blockAuth = b
  /\ shuttle = 0
  /\ k <= parked[b]
  /\ parked' = [parked EXCEPT ![b] = parked[b] - k]
  /\ shuttle' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<berth, areaAuth, blockAuth>>

SetDown(b) ==
  /\ blockAuth = b
  /\ shuttle > 0
  /\ parked[b] + shuttle <= berth[b]
  /\ parked' = [parked EXCEPT ![b] = parked[b] + shuttle]
  /\ shuttle' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<berth, areaAuth, blockAuth>>

\* A berth allowance is paperwork: re-rating it must never be allowed to
\* leave stock that is already parked outside the books.
Rerate(b, c) ==
  /\ areaAuth = AreaOf(b)
  /\ c >= parked[b]
  /\ berth' = [berth EXCEPT ![b] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<parked, areaAuth, blockAuth, shuttle>>

ReleaseAuth ==
  /\ areaAuth # NoArea
  /\ areaAuth' = NoArea
  /\ blockAuth' = NoBlock
  /\ UNCHANGED <<parked, berth, shuttle>>

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Areas : TakeArea(a)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : TakeBlock(b)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks, k \in 1 .. FleetSize : LiftOnto(b, k)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : SetDown(b)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks, c \in MinBerth .. MaxBerth : Rerate(b, c)
  \/ ReleaseAuth

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The closed-system claim: every car is either parked in some block or
\* riding the shuttle, and the two together always add up to the fleet.
FleetConserved == OnTrack + shuttle = FleetSize
===========================================================================

CONSTANTS
    NumBlocks = 3
    SplitAt = 1
    FleetSize = 2
    MinBerth = 1
    MaxBerth = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT FleetConserved
nl:
A metro operator tracks rolling stock across a signalling territory that is divided into track blocks, and the blocks are grouped into two interlocking areas, a northern area and a southern area. Every car of rolling stock sits either parked in one of the track blocks or riding on the single shunting shuttle that moves stock between blocks. The dispatcher's whole concern here is bookkeeping: the territory is a closed system for the shift, so the fleet on the territory is fixed and no car may be conjured up or quietly lost as stock is shuffled around.

Because the interlocking hardware is layered, a movement is authorised in two steps. The dispatcher first takes the area-level authority for one of the two interlocking areas, and only once that coarse authority is held may the dispatcher take the block-level authority for one specific block inside that area. Only one area authority and one block authority are outstanding at a time; both are given back together when the movement is finished.

With the block authority in hand the dispatcher may lift a number of cars out of that block onto the shunting shuttle, which must be empty to receive them, and the block loses exactly the cars that the shuttle gains. Later, holding the block authority for some block, the dispatcher may set the loaded shuttle down into that block, provided the block's current berth allowance can absorb every car on the shuttle; the block gains exactly what the shuttle was carrying and the shuttle goes empty. Berth allowances are not fixed for the shift: while holding the area authority the dispatcher may re-rate a block's berth allowance up or down, but a re-rating may never be set below the number of cars already parked in that block, because a re-rating is a paperwork change and must never push stock off the books.

The full action set is: take the area authority for an interlocking area, take the block authority for a block inside the currently authorised area, lift some cars from the authorised block onto the empty shuttle, set the loaded shuttle down into the authorised block when its berth allowance can absorb them, re-rate the berth allowance of a block in the authorised area without going below its current occupancy, and give back both authorities together.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars parked across all track blocks plus the number of cars riding on the shunting shuttle always equals the fixed size of the fleet assigned to the territory, so no car is ever created or destroyed by a shunt or by a berth re-rating.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m2p3t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Players, Regions, NumSlots

Slots == 1 .. NumSlots
NoPlayer == "empty"
NoSeat == 0
NoTxn == [pl |-> NoPlayer, sl |-> NoSeat]

VARIABLES phase, txn, ballot, occupant, seat
vars == <<phase, txn, ballot, occupant, seat>>

AllBalloted == \A r \in Regions : ballot[r] # "open"
Unanimous == \A r \in Regions : ballot[r] = "yes"

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in {"idle", "balloting", "committing", "aborting"}
  /\ txn \in [pl : Players \cup {NoPlayer}, sl : Slots \cup {NoSeat}]
  /\ ballot \in [Regions -> {"open", "yes", "no"}]
  /\ occupant \in [Slots -> Players \cup {NoPlayer}]
  /\ seat \in [Players -> Slots \cup {NoSeat}]

Init ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ txn = NoTxn
  /\ ballot = [r \in Regions |-> "open"]
  /\ occupant = [s \in Slots |-> NoPlayer]
  /\ seat = [p \in Players |-> NoSeat]

Propose(p, s) ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ seat[p] = NoSeat
  /\ phase' = "balloting"
  /\ txn' = [pl |-> p, sl |-> s]
  /\ ballot' = [r \in Regions |-> "open"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, seat>>

\* A region server answers from its own lobby view; it is slow but never
\* silent, so the coordinator waits for every ballot instead of timing out.
CastBallot(r) ==
  /\ phase = "balloting"
  /\ ballot[r] = "open"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![r] =
        IF occupant[txn.sl] = NoPlayer /\ seat[txn.pl] = NoSeat
          THEN "yes" ELSE "no"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, txn, occupant, seat>>

DecideCommit ==
  /\ phase = "balloting"
  /\ AllBalloted
  /\ Unanimous
  /\ occupant[txn.sl] = NoPlayer
  /\ phase' = "committing"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<txn, ballot, occupant, seat>>

DecideAbort ==
  /\ phase = "balloting"
  /\ AllBalloted
  /\ ~(Unanimous /\ occupant[txn.sl] = NoPlayer)
  /\ phase' = "aborting"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<txn, ballot, occupant, seat>>

Decide == DecideCommit \/ DecideAbort

ApplySeating ==
  /\ phase = "committing"
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![txn.sl] = txn.pl]
  /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![txn.pl] = txn.sl]
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ txn' = NoTxn
  /\ UNCHANGED ballot

CloseAbort ==
  /\ phase = "aborting"
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ txn' = NoTxn
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, occupant, seat>>

StandUp(p) ==
  /\ seat[p] # NoSeat
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![seat[p]] = NoPlayer]
  /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![p] = NoSeat]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, txn, ballot>>

BallotAny == \E r \in Regions : CastBallot(r)

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots : Propose(p, s)
  \/ BallotAny
  \/ Decide
  \/ ApplySeating
  \/ CloseAbort
  \/ \E p \in Players : StandUp(p)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(BallotAny)
  /\ WF_vars(Decide)
  /\ WF_vars(ApplySeating)
  /\ WF_vars(CloseAbort)

\* Two-directional agreement between the slot side and the player side of
\* the seating map: this is what rules out one slot holding two players.
SeatingCoherent ==
  /\ \A p \in Players : seat[p] # NoSeat => occupant[seat[p]] = p
  /\ \A s \in Slots : occupant[s] # NoPlayer => seat[occupant[s]] = s

\* Slow participants still answer, so no transaction hangs in balloting.
EveryTransactionDecides ==
  (phase = "balloting") ~> (phase = "idle")
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Players = {pa, pb}
    Regions = {r1, r2}
    NumSlots = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SeatingCoherent

PROPERTY EveryTransactionDecides
nl:
An online game runs a lobby matchmaker. A lobby has a fixed number of numbered player slots, and seating a player into a slot has to be agreed by every region server that mirrors the lobby, because each region server serves the lobby view to its own players. The matchmaker acts as the transaction coordinator and runs one seating transaction at a time.

A seating transaction begins when the matchmaker proposes to seat a currently unseated player into a particular slot; the proposal is recorded and every region server's ballot is cleared. Each region server then casts its ballot on the open proposal. A region server casts a yes ballot when, according to the lobby view it holds, the proposed slot has nobody in it and the proposed player is not already seated somewhere; otherwise it casts a no ballot. The region servers are known to be slow but not failed: a server may take arbitrarily long to answer, but it always answers eventually, which is why the matchmaker simply waits rather than timing anybody out.

Once every region server has balloted, the matchmaker takes the decision. It moves the transaction into the committing phase only if every ballot was yes and the proposed slot is still empty at decision time; otherwise it moves the transaction into the aborting phase. Committing writes the seating through: the slot records the player as its occupant and the player records the slot as its seat, and the transaction closes. Aborting simply closes the transaction and leaves the lobby untouched. Separately, a seated player may stand up at any time, which clears both the slot's occupant record and the player's seat record.

The full action set is: propose a seating of an unseated player into a slot, cast a region server's ballot on the open proposal, take the commit-or-abort decision once all ballots are in, apply a committed seating, close an aborted transaction, and stand a seated player up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot occupancy records and the player seating records always agree with each other in both directions, so a player's recorded seat always names a slot that records that same player as its occupant and vice versa, which means no slot is ever allocated to two different players at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every seating transaction that reaches the balloting phase eventually reaches a decision and closes.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m9p0t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, Crews, CompanyACrews, MaxEpoch

Companies == {"A", "B"}
NoCrew == "nobody"
Epochs == 0 .. MaxEpoch

CompanyOf(c) == IF c \in CompanyACrews THEN "A" ELSE "B"

VARIABLES epoch, assignment, lockHolder, lockEpoch, vaultOpen
vars == <<epoch, assignment, lockHolder, lockEpoch, vaultOpen>>

QuietNetwork == \A m \in Machines : vaultOpen[m] = NoCrew

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in Epochs
  /\ assignment \in [Machines -> Companies]
  /\ lockHolder \in [Machines -> Crews \cup {NoCrew}]
  /\ lockEpoch \in [Machines -> Epochs]
  /\ vaultOpen \in [Machines -> Crews \cup {NoCrew}]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ assignment = [m \in Machines |-> "A"]
  /\ lockHolder = [m \in Machines |-> NoCrew]
  /\ lockEpoch = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ vaultOpen = [m \in Machines |-> NoCrew]

\* A reconfiguration republishes the whole territory map and bumps the epoch;
\* it is only allowed in a quiet window with every vault shut.
Reconfigure(newmap) ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ QuietNetwork
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ assignment' = newmap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lockHolder, lockEpoch, vaultOpen>>

\* A lock stamped with an older epoch is stale and may be reclaimed.
TakeLock(m, c) ==
  /\ vaultOpen[m] = NoCrew
  /\ assignment[m] = CompanyOf(c)
  /\ \/ lockHolder[m] = NoCrew
     \/ lockEpoch[m] < epoch
  /\ lockHolder' = [lockHolder EXCEPT ![m] = c]
  /\ lockEpoch' = [lockEpoch EXCEPT ![m] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assignment, vaultOpen>>

OpenVault(m, c) ==
  /\ lockHolder[m] = c
  /\ lockEpoch[m] = epoch
  /\ vaultOpen[m] = NoCrew
  /\ vaultOpen' = [vaultOpen EXCEPT ![m] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assignment, lockHolder, lockEpoch>>

ShutVault(m) ==
  /\ vaultOpen[m] # NoCrew
  /\ vaultOpen' = [vaultOpen EXCEPT ![m] = NoCrew]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assignment, lockHolder, lockEpoch>>

GiveBackLock(m) ==
  /\ lockHolder[m] # NoCrew
  /\ vaultOpen[m] = NoCrew
  /\ lockHolder' = [lockHolder EXCEPT ![m] = NoCrew]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assignment, lockEpoch, vaultOpen>>

Next ==
  \/ \E newmap \in [Machines -> Companies] : Reconfigure(newmap)
  \/ \E m \in Machines, c \in Crews : TakeLock(m, c)
  \/ \E m \in Machines, c \in Crews : OpenVault(m, c)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : ShutVault(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : GiveBackLock(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anyone inside an open machine must be its current lock holder, holding a
\* stamp from the live epoch, and working for the company that owns it now.
OccupancyAuthorised ==
  \A m \in Machines :
    vaultOpen[m] # NoCrew =>
      /\ lockHolder[m] = vaultOpen[m]
      /\ lockEpoch[m] = epoch
      /\ assignment[m] = CompanyOf(vaultOpen[m])
===========================================================================
nl:
A regional vending machine network is looked after by two independent field operations companies, company A and company B, which draw from one shared pool of machines rather than owning fixed territories. Each company sends out its own service crews. Inside every machine is a cash vault, and an open vault is a critical resource: while one crew has a machine's vault open, no other crew may be inside that same machine, whichever company it belongs to.

Which company is responsible for which machine is decided by a network-wide configuration that carries an epoch number. A reconfiguration bumps the epoch and republishes the whole machine-to-company assignment at once. Reconfiguration is only permitted during a quiet window in which no vault anywhere on the network is open, and the epoch counter only runs up to a fixed planning horizon.

Before touching a machine a crew must take that machine's service lock. A crew may take the lock when the machine currently has no lock holder, or when the machine's lock was stamped with an epoch older than the current one and is therefore stale and reclaimable; either way the crew may only take the lock on a machine that the current configuration assigns to that crew's own company, and only while the machine's vault is shut. Taking the lock stamps it with the current epoch.

A crew may open a machine's vault only while it is the recorded lock holder for that machine, its lock stamp matches the current epoch, and the vault is shut. Any open vault may afterwards be shut again. A crew holding a lock may give the lock back once the vault is shut.

The full action set is: reconfigure the network during a quiet window by bumping the epoch and republishing the assignment, take a machine's service lock when it is free or stale and the machine belongs to the crew's company, open the vault of a machine whose current-epoch lock the crew holds, shut an open vault, and give back a service lock while the vault is shut.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a machine's vault is open, the crew inside it is that machine's recorded lock holder, its lock stamp carries the current configuration epoch, and the machine is assigned to that crew's own company in the current configuration, so no second crew and no stale or out-of-territory crew is ever inside an open machine.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m7p0t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, MaxVersion, MaxAllowance

Nobody == "nobody"
Versions == 0 .. MaxVersion

VARIABLES regHolder, regVersion, phase, claimTicket, allowance
vars == <<regHolder, regVersion, phase, claimTicket, allowance>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ regHolder \in Machines \cup {Nobody}
  /\ regVersion \in Versions
  /\ phase \in [Machines -> {"quiet", "trying", "claimant", "refilling"}]
  /\ claimTicket \in [Machines -> Versions]
  /\ allowance \in 0 .. MaxAllowance

Init ==
  /\ regHolder = Nobody
  /\ regVersion = 0
  /\ phase = [m \in Machines |-> "quiet"]
  /\ claimTicket = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ allowance = MaxAllowance

Announce(m) ==
  /\ phase[m] = "quiet"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "trying"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regHolder, regVersion, claimTicket, allowance>>

\* The swap succeeds only against a holder field reading nobody; the winner
\* privately records the version it wrote as its claim ticket.
Swap(m) ==
  /\ phase[m] \in {"trying", "claimant"}
  /\ regHolder = Nobody
  /\ regVersion < MaxVersion
  /\ regHolder' = m
  /\ regVersion' = regVersion + 1
  /\ claimTicket' = [claimTicket EXCEPT ![m] = regVersion + 1]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "claimant"]
  /\ UNCHANGED allowance

RollIn(m) ==
  /\ phase[m] = "claimant"
  /\ regHolder = m
  /\ claimTicket[m] = regVersion
  /\ allowance > 0
  /\ allowance' = allowance - 1
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "refilling"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regHolder, regVersion, claimTicket>>

RollOut(m) ==
  /\ phase[m] = "refilling"
  /\ regHolder' = Nobody
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "quiet"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regVersion, claimTicket, allowance>>

\* Revoking bumps the version, which silently staled the old ticket.
Revoke(m) ==
  /\ regHolder = m
  /\ phase[m] = "claimant"
  /\ regVersion < MaxVersion
  /\ regHolder' = Nobody
  /\ regVersion' = regVersion + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, claimTicket, allowance>>

Raise ==
  /\ allowance < MaxAllowance
  /\ allowance' = allowance + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regHolder, regVersion, phase, claimTicket>>

Cut ==
  /\ allowance > 0
  /\ allowance' = allowance - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regHolder, regVersion, phase, claimTicket>>

RollInAny == \E m \in Machines : RollIn(m)
RollOutAny == \E m \in Machines : RollOut(m)

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Announce(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Swap(m)
  \/ RollInAny
  \/ RollOutAny
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Revoke(m)
  \/ Raise
  \/ Cut

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(RollInAny)
  /\ WF_vars(RollOutAny)
  /\ WF_vars(Raise)

\* Occupancy must be backed by a live, unsuperseded claim ticket.
DockClaimLive ==
  \A m \in Machines :
    phase[m] = "refilling" => /\ regHolder = m
                              /\ claimTicket[m] = regVersion

\* The dock is never held forever: a claimed register always frees again.
DockAlwaysFreesUp == (regHolder # Nobody) ~> (regHolder = Nobody)
===========================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Machines = {v1, v2}
    MaxVersion = 3
    MaxAllowance = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT DockClaimLive

PROPERTY DockAlwaysFreesUp
nl:
A vending machine network shares one physical coin-refill dock at the depot. Only one machine may be standing in the dock being refilled at any moment, so the dock is the network's critical resource. Access to it is arbitrated entirely through a single compare-and-swap register at the depot controller. The register carries two fields: the identity of the machine that currently holds the dock claim, and a version counter that is bumped on every successful swap. The version counter only runs up to a fixed ceiling before the controller stops accepting swaps.

A machine that wants coins first announces that it is trying. A trying machine, or a machine that still believes it holds a claim that has since been swapped away, may attempt the compare-and-swap: if the register's holder field currently reads nobody, the machine swaps its own identity in, the version counter goes up by one, and the machine privately writes down the version it just wrote as its claim ticket. A machine that has swapped itself in is a claimant.

A claimant may actually roll into the dock and start refilling only if the register still names it as holder and its private claim ticket still matches the register's live version, and only if the depot's refill allowance for the shift is greater than zero; rolling in consumes one unit of that allowance. When the refill is finished the machine rolls out and the register's holder field is set back to nobody.

The depot controller may also revoke a claim that is only a claim: if a machine holds the register but has not yet rolled into the dock, the controller may swap the holder field back to nobody and bump the version, which silently invalidates that machine's claim ticket. The refill allowance is not a fixed number for the shift: the depot may raise it by one at any time and may also cut it by one at any time, so the capacity available to the network genuinely changes while the network is running. The depot always does eventually top the allowance back up when it is below its ceiling.

The full action set is: announce a machine as trying, compare-and-swap the register to claim the dock, roll into the dock and begin refilling against a live claim and a positive allowance, finish refilling and release the register, revoke an unused claim by swapping the holder back to nobody with a version bump, raise the refill allowance by one, and cut the refill allowance by one.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any machine that is actually in the dock refilling is named as holder by the compare-and-swap register and its private claim ticket equals the register's live version, so a machine whose claim was revoked or superseded can never be the one occupying the dock and two machines can never be refilling at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the compare-and-swap register names some machine as holder of the dock, the register eventually reads nobody again.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m4p2t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Jobs, ListLimit

Spoolers == {"A", "B"}
NoJob == "idlepress"

VARIABLES pool, worklist, press, archive, backpressure
vars == <<pool, worklist, press, archive, backpressure>>

CopiesOnList(i, j) == Cardinality({k \in 1 .. Len(worklist[i]) : worklist[i][k] = j})

\* Custody count for one job across pool, both work lists, both presses
\* and the archive; the shop's books require this to be exactly one.
Custodies(j) ==
  (IF j \in pool THEN 1 ELSE 0)
    + CopiesOnList("A", j)
    + CopiesOnList("B", j)
    + Cardinality({i \in Spoolers : press[i] = j})
    + (IF j \in archive THEN 1 ELSE 0)

TypeOK ==
  /\ pool \subseteq Jobs
  /\ archive \subseteq Jobs
  /\ press \in [Spoolers -> Jobs \cup {NoJob}]
  /\ backpressure \in [Spoolers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ pool = Jobs
  /\ worklist = [i \in Spoolers |-> <<>>]
  /\ press = [i \in Spoolers |-> NoJob]
  /\ archive = {}
  /\ backpressure = [i \in Spoolers |-> FALSE]

ClaimJob(i, j) ==
  /\ j \in pool
  /\ ~backpressure[i]
  /\ Len(worklist[i]) < ListLimit
  /\ pool' = pool \ {j}
  /\ worklist' = [worklist EXCEPT ![i] = Append(worklist[i], j)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<press, archive, backpressure>>

\* Backpressure is the spooler refusing new work while its list is full.
RaiseBackpressure(i) ==
  /\ ~backpressure[i]
  /\ Len(worklist[i]) >= ListLimit
  /\ backpressure' = [backpressure EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, worklist, press, archive>>

DropBackpressure(i) ==
  /\ backpressure[i]
  /\ Len(worklist[i]) < ListLimit
  /\ backpressure' = [backpressure EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, worklist, press, archive>>

LoadPress(i) ==
  /\ press[i] = NoJob
  /\ Len(worklist[i]) > 0
  /\ press' = [press EXCEPT ![i] = Head(worklist[i])]
  /\ worklist' = [worklist EXCEPT ![i] = Tail(worklist[i])]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, archive, backpressure>>

CompleteJob(i) ==
  /\ press[i] # NoJob
  /\ archive' = archive \cup {press[i]}
  /\ press' = [press EXCEPT ![i] = NoJob]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, worklist, backpressure>>

\* An archived job can be pulled back for a reprint, so the shop's job
\* population keeps circulating rather than settling in the archive.
ReprintRequest(j) ==
  /\ j \in archive
  /\ archive' = archive \ {j}
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<worklist, press, backpressure>>

AbortToPool(i) ==
  /\ press[i] # NoJob
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {press[i]}
  /\ press' = [press EXCEPT ![i] = NoJob]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<worklist, archive, backpressure>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Spoolers, j \in Jobs : ClaimJob(i, j)
  \/ \E i \in Spoolers : RaiseBackpressure(i)
  \/ \E i \in Spoolers : DropBackpressure(i)
  \/ \E i \in Spoolers : LoadPress(i)
  \/ \E i \in Spoolers : CompleteJob(i)
  \/ \E i \in Spoolers : AbortToPool(i)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : ReprintRequest(j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nothing created, nothing destroyed: one custody per job, always.
CustodyExactlyOnce == \A j \in Jobs : Custodies(j) = 1
===========================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Jobs = {j1, j2, j3}
    ListLimit = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CustodyExactlyOnce
nl:
A commercial print shop runs two independent spooler instances, instance A and instance B, in front of one shared pool of submitted print jobs. Neither spooler owns a territory; both reach into the same pool of unclaimed jobs. Each spooler keeps its own bounded work list, and each spooler drives its own press.

The shop's accounting rule is that a submitted job is a physical thing that must exist in exactly one custody at any moment: it is either sitting unclaimed in the shared pool, or waiting on exactly one spooler's work list, or loaded on exactly one press, or filed in the completed archive. A job must never be duplicated so that two spoolers both think they are carrying it, and it must never fall out of every custody and vanish.

A spooler may take an unclaimed job out of the pool and put it on the end of its own work list, but only if that work list is below its length limit and the spooler is not currently signalling backpressure. When a spooler's work list has reached its length limit it may raise a backpressure signal, which refuses further claims from the pool; once the work list has drained back below the limit the spooler may drop the backpressure signal again. A spooler with an idle press may pull the job at the front of its work list off the list and load it onto its press. A press that has finished stamps its job into the completed archive and goes idle. A spooler may also abort a job that is on its press, which takes the job off the press and returns it to the shared pool for either spooler to pick up later. Finally, a customer may raise a reprint request against a job that is already filed in the completed archive, which pulls that job out of the archive and back into the shared unclaimed pool.

The full action set is: claim an unclaimed job from the shared pool onto a spooler's work list, raise a spooler's backpressure signal when its work list is at its limit, drop the backpressure signal once the work list is under the limit, load the front job of a work list onto that spooler's idle press, complete a press job into the archive, abort a press job back into the shared pool, and pull an archived job back into the shared pool as a reprint request.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every submitted job has exactly one custody at all times, counting the shared pool, the two spoolers' work lists, the two presses, and the completed archive, so no job is ever duplicated into two custodies and none is ever lost from all of them.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m4p4t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Chutes, BerthAllowance, TotalBags

Counts == 0 .. TotalBags

VARIABLES feeder, committed, standing, handlerUp, holdOff
vars == <<feeder, committed, standing, handlerUp, holdOff>>

\* Committed bags are still on the belt but already count against the berth.
Charged(c) == standing[c] + committed[c]

TypeOK ==
  /\ feeder \in Counts
  /\ committed \in [Chutes -> Counts]
  /\ standing \in [Chutes -> Counts]
  /\ handlerUp \in [Chutes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ holdOff \in [Chutes -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ feeder = TotalBags
  /\ committed = [c \in Chutes |-> 0]
  /\ standing = [c \in Chutes |-> 0]
  /\ handlerUp = [c \in Chutes |-> TRUE]
  /\ holdOff = [c \in Chutes |-> FALSE]

Dispatch(c) ==
  /\ feeder > 0
  /\ ~holdOff[c]
  /\ Charged(c) < BerthAllowance
  /\ feeder' = feeder - 1
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![c] = committed[c] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<standing, handlerUp, holdOff>>

RollOff(c) ==
  /\ committed[c] > 0
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![c] = committed[c] - 1]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = standing[c] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, handlerUp, holdOff>>

PullForOnward(c) ==
  /\ handlerUp[c]
  /\ standing[c] > 0
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = standing[c] - 1]
  /\ feeder' = feeder + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, handlerUp, holdOff>>

RaiseHoldOff(c) ==
  /\ ~holdOff[c]
  /\ Charged(c) >= BerthAllowance
  /\ holdOff' = [holdOff EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, committed, standing, handlerUp>>

DropHoldOff(c) ==
  /\ holdOff[c]
  /\ Charged(c) < BerthAllowance
  /\ holdOff' = [holdOff EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, committed, standing, handlerUp>>

\* Exactly one handler in the hall may fail, and it leaves no trace when
\* it does; the router's berth accounting has to stand on its own.
CrashHandler(c) ==
  /\ \A d \in Chutes : handlerUp[d]
  /\ handlerUp' = [handlerUp EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, committed, standing, holdOff>>

HandDrag(c) ==
  /\ ~handlerUp[c]
  /\ standing[c] > 0
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = standing[c] - 1]
  /\ feeder' = feeder + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, handlerUp, holdOff>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : Dispatch(c)
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : RollOff(c)
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : PullForOnward(c)
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : RaiseHoldOff(c)
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : DropHoldOff(c)
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : CrashHandler(c)
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : HandDrag(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The berth allowance is charged against arrived and in-flight bags alike.
BerthNeverOversubscribed ==
  \A c \in Chutes : standing[c] + committed[c] <= BerthAllowance

CONSTANTS
    Chutes = {c1, c2}
    BerthAllowance = 2
    TotalBags = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BerthNeverOversubscribed
nl:
An airport baggage router feeds bags from a central check-in feeder onto a belt that carries them to a small number of make-up chutes. Every chute has a hard berth allowance: the number of bags physically standing in the chute plus the number of bags already committed to that chute and still riding the belt must never exceed the allowance, because a chute that overflows dumps luggage onto the floor of the make-up hall.

The router therefore accounts for committed bags, not just arrived ones. It may only dispatch a bag from the feeder toward a chute when the feeder is not empty, the chute is not currently signalling backpressure, and the chute's arrived-plus-committed count is strictly below its berth allowance; dispatching moves the bag off the feeder and onto the belt as a commitment against that chute. A bag riding the belt eventually rolls off into its chute, turning a commitment into a standing bag.

Each chute is worked by its own handler. A live handler may pull a standing bag out of its chute and send it back round to the feeder for its onward flight. A chute may raise a backpressure signal once its arrived-plus-committed count has reached the berth allowance, and may drop that signal again once the count has fallen below the allowance.

One handler in the hall can crash silently: at most one handler ever fails, it fails without announcing anything, and nothing in the router's records changes when it does. A crashed handler simply stops pulling bags out of its chute, so bags accumulate there and the router must keep respecting that chute's allowance purely on the strength of its own accounting. A supervisor may walk over and drag a bag off a dead chute by hand, returning it to the feeder.

The full action set is: dispatch a bag from the feeder as a commitment to a chute that has room and is not signalling backpressure, roll a committed bag off the belt into its chute, have a live handler pull a standing bag from its chute back to the feeder, raise a chute's backpressure signal once it is at its allowance, drop a chute's backpressure signal once it is below its allowance, crash the one handler that is allowed to fail, and have a supervisor hand-drag a bag off a dead chute back to the feeder.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every chute, the number of bags standing in it plus the number of bags committed to it and still on the belt never exceeds that chute's berth allowance, even when a handler has silently crashed and stopped draining.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m7p3t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Containers, NumSlots

Slots == 1 .. NumSlots
Planners == {"A", "B"}
FreeReg == "free"
NoSlot == 0
EmptyHand == "emptyhand"

VARIABLES waitingPool, inHand, slotReg, yardPlan, landed
vars == <<waitingPool, inHand, slotReg, yardPlan, landed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ waitingPool \in [Containers -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ landed \in [Containers -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ inHand \in [Planners -> Containers \cup {EmptyHand}]
  /\ slotReg \in [Slots -> Containers \cup {FreeReg}]
  /\ yardPlan \in [Containers -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]

Init ==
  /\ waitingPool = [k \in Containers |-> TRUE]
  /\ inHand = [p \in Planners |-> EmptyHand]
  /\ slotReg = [s \in Slots |-> FreeReg]
  /\ yardPlan = [k \in Containers |-> NoSlot]
  /\ landed = [k \in Containers |-> FALSE]

TakeFromPool(p, k) ==
  /\ inHand[p] = EmptyHand
  /\ waitingPool[k]
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![p] = k]
  /\ waitingPool' = [waitingPool EXCEPT ![k] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotReg, yardPlan, landed>>

PutBack(p) ==
  /\ inHand[p] # EmptyHand
  /\ yardPlan[inHand[p]] = NoSlot
  /\ waitingPool' = [waitingPool EXCEPT ![inHand[p]] = TRUE]
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![p] = EmptyHand]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotReg, yardPlan, landed>>

\* Compare the slot register against "free" and, only on a match, swap the
\* container's identity in; the failing comparison is what blocks the rival.
CompareAndSwap(p, s) ==
  /\ inHand[p] # EmptyHand
  /\ yardPlan[inHand[p]] = NoSlot
  /\ slotReg[s] = FreeReg
  /\ slotReg' = [slotReg EXCEPT ![s] = inHand[p]]
  /\ yardPlan' = [yardPlan EXCEPT ![inHand[p]] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waitingPool, inHand, landed>>

Land(p) ==
  /\ inHand[p] # EmptyHand
  /\ yardPlan[inHand[p]] # NoSlot
  /\ landed' = [landed EXCEPT ![inHand[p]] = TRUE]
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![p] = EmptyHand]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waitingPool, slotReg, yardPlan>>

LiftOut(k) ==
  /\ landed[k]
  /\ landed' = [landed EXCEPT ![k] = FALSE]
  /\ slotReg' = [slotReg EXCEPT ![yardPlan[k]] = FreeReg]
  /\ yardPlan' = [yardPlan EXCEPT ![k] = NoSlot]
  /\ waitingPool' = [waitingPool EXCEPT ![k] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED inHand

LandA == Land("A")
LandB == Land("B")

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Planners, k \in Containers : TakeFromPool(p, k)
  \/ \E p \in Planners : PutBack(p)
  \/ \E p \in Planners, s \in Slots : CompareAndSwap(p, s)
  \/ LandA
  \/ LandB
  \/ \E k \in Containers : LiftOut(k)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(LandA)
  /\ WF_vars(LandB)

\* A planned slot always reads back the very container that planned it, so
\* no two containers can be allocated the same stack position.
PlanMatchesRegister ==
  \A k \in Containers :
    yardPlan[k] # NoSlot => slotReg[yardPlan[k]] = k

\* Each planner keeps working its own container, so a claimed slot is used.
PlannedContainerLands ==
  \A k \in Containers : (yardPlan[k] # NoSlot) ~> (landed[k] = TRUE)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Containers = {k1, k2}
    NumSlots = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT PlanMatchesRegister

PROPERTY PlannedContainerLands
nl:
A container terminal has one yard of numbered stack slots, and two independent yard-planning instances, planner A and planner B, both draw work from the same shared pool of containers waiting to be landed. Neither planner owns a region of the yard; both reach into the same pool and both compete for the same slots.

Each slot in the yard has its own compare-and-swap register at the terminal operating system. The register reads either "free" or the identity of the container that owns the slot. A planner claims a slot by comparing the register against "free" and, only if that comparison holds, swapping the container's identity into it in the same indivisible step, while writing the slot number into the container's yard-plan entry. If the register does not read "free" the comparison fails and no claim is made, which is how the second planner is stopped from taking a slot the first has already swapped itself into.

A planner with a free hand may take any container out of the shared waiting pool and start working it. A planner may also put a container it has not yet found a slot for back into the shared pool. A planner whose container has a slot number in its yard-plan entry may bring the crane over and land the container, after which the planner's hand is free again and the container is recorded as landed in the yard. Later a landed container may be lifted out for its onward voyage, which swaps its slot register back to "free", clears its yard-plan entry, and returns the container to the shared waiting pool.

The full action set is: take a container from the shared pool with a free hand, put an unplaced container back into the shared pool, compare-and-swap a free slot register to claim it for the container in hand, land a container that holds a slot, and lift a landed container back out to the pool while freeing its slot register.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a container's yard-plan entry names a slot, that slot's compare-and-swap register reads exactly that container, so two different containers can never end up allocated to the same yard slot.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every container that has been given a slot in its yard-plan entry is eventually landed in the yard.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m9p4t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Fridges, Couriers, MaxUnits, MinAllowance, MaxAllowance, MaxEpoch

Epochs == 0 .. MaxEpoch
NoFridge == "unbooked"
Allowances == MinAllowance .. MaxAllowance

VARIABLES epoch, allowance, stored, booking, onRoad
vars == <<epoch, allowance, stored, booking, onRoad>>

\* Only bookings carrying the live epoch still hold a berth; a reconfiguration
\* stales every outstanding booking in one step.
LiveBookings(f) ==
  Cardinality({c \in Couriers : booking[c].fridge = f /\ booking[c].ep = epoch})

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in Epochs
  /\ allowance \in [Fridges -> Allowances]
  /\ stored \in [Fridges -> 0 .. MaxUnits]
  /\ booking \in [Couriers -> [fridge : Fridges \cup {NoFridge}, ep : Epochs]]
  /\ onRoad \in [Couriers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ allowance = [f \in Fridges |-> MaxAllowance]
  /\ stored = [f \in Fridges |-> 0]
  /\ booking = [c \in Couriers |-> [fridge |-> NoFridge, ep |-> 0]]
  /\ onRoad = [c \in Couriers |-> TRUE]

BookBerth(c, f) ==
  /\ onRoad[c]
  /\ booking[c].fridge = NoFridge
  /\ stored[f] + LiveBookings(f) < allowance[f]
  /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![c] = [fridge |-> f, ep |-> epoch]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, allowance, stored, onRoad>>

BringUnitIn(c) ==
  /\ onRoad[c]
  /\ booking[c].fridge # NoFridge
  /\ booking[c].ep = epoch
  /\ stored' = [stored EXCEPT ![booking[c].fridge] = stored[booking[c].fridge] + 1]
  /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![c] = [fridge |-> NoFridge, ep |-> epoch]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, allowance, onRoad>>

HandBookingBack(c) ==
  /\ onRoad[c]
  /\ booking[c].fridge # NoFridge
  /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![c] = [fridge |-> NoFridge, ep |-> epoch]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, allowance, stored, onRoad>>

DrawForTransfusion(f) ==
  /\ stored[f] > 0
  /\ stored' = [stored EXCEPT ![f] = stored[f] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, allowance, booking, onRoad>>

\* A republished plan must still cover everything already on the shelves.
Reconfigure(plan) ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \A f \in Fridges : plan[f] >= stored[f]
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ allowance' = plan
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stored, booking, onRoad>>

\* Exactly one courier may go dark, and it leaves its booking dangling.
GoDark(c) ==
  /\ \A d \in Couriers : onRoad[d]
  /\ onRoad' = [onRoad EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, allowance, stored, booking>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Couriers, f \in Fridges : BookBerth(c, f)
  \/ \E c \in Couriers : BringUnitIn(c)
  \/ \E c \in Couriers : HandBookingBack(c)
  \/ \E f \in Fridges : DrawForTransfusion(f)
  \/ \E plan \in [Fridges -> Allowances] : Reconfigure(plan)
  \/ \E c \in Couriers : GoDark(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Shelf space is charged to stored units and live bookings together.
AllowanceNeverOverbooked ==
  \A f \in Fridges : stored[f] + LiveBookings(f) <= allowance[f]
===========================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Fridges = {f1, f2}
    Couriers = {c1, c2}
    MaxUnits = 2
    MinAllowance = 1
    MaxAllowance = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT AllowanceNeverOverbooked
nl:
A regional blood bank tracks stored units across a set of cold-storage fridges. Every fridge has a rated shelf allowance, and the bank's rule is that the units physically inside a fridge plus the units that couriers have booked space for, but not yet brought in, must never exceed that fridge's allowance. Overbooking a fridge means a courier arrives with cold product and no berth for it.

The fridge allowance plan is published under a configuration epoch. A reconfiguration bumps the epoch and republishes the whole allowance plan in one step; the epoch counter runs up to a fixed planning horizon. A reconfiguration is only accepted if every fridge's newly published allowance is at least the number of units already sitting in that fridge, and bumping the epoch invalidates every outstanding booking at a stroke, because a booking is only honoured while it carries the live epoch.

A live courier with no outstanding booking may book space in a fridge, provided the units already inside plus the bookings that still carry the live epoch leave at least one berth free; the booking is stamped with the epoch that was live when it was made. A live courier holding a booking stamped with the live epoch may bring its unit in, which puts one more unit inside the fridge and consumes the booking. A live courier may also simply hand a booking back. Units are drawn out of a fridge for transfusion whenever the fridge is not empty.

One courier on the road can crash silently: at most one courier ever goes dark, it does so without telling the bank anything, and its booking is left dangling. Nothing in the bank's records marks the courier as gone, so the dangling booking keeps consuming a berth until the next reconfiguration bumps the epoch and stales it.

The full action set is: book a berth in a fridge for a live courier when the live-epoch accounting leaves room, bring a booked unit into its fridge under a live-epoch booking, hand a booking back, draw a unit out of a non-empty fridge, reconfigure the allowance plan by bumping the epoch to allowances that cover what is already stored, and crash the one courier that is allowed to go dark.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every fridge, the units stored inside it plus the outstanding bookings against it that still carry the live configuration epoch never exceed that fridge's published shelf allowance.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m0p4t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Desks, Ceiling, LegSize

NoDesk == "unflagged"
Amounts == 0 .. Ceiling

VARIABLES drawn, worksheet, desk, flagged, posted
vars == <<drawn, worksheet, desk, flagged, posted>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ drawn \in Amounts
  /\ worksheet \in [Desks -> Amounts]
  /\ desk \in [Desks -> {"standby", "prepared"}]
  /\ flagged \in Desks \cup {NoDesk}
  /\ posted \in [Desks -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ drawn = 0
  /\ worksheet = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
  /\ desk = [d \in Desks |-> "standby"]
  /\ flagged = NoDesk
  /\ posted = [d \in Desks |-> FALSE]

\* Preparing takes a snapshot, and it is refused unless the figure just read
\* already leaves room for a leg; that check is what the push relies on.
PrepareLeg(d) ==
  /\ desk[d] = "standby"
  /\ drawn + LegSize <= Ceiling
  /\ worksheet' = [worksheet EXCEPT ![d] = drawn]
  /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d] = "prepared"]
  /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drawn, flagged>>

\* The optimistic push: the snapshot must still equal the live figure.
PushThrough(d) ==
  /\ desk[d] = "prepared"
  /\ flagged # d
  /\ worksheet[d] = drawn
  /\ drawn' = worksheet[d] + LegSize
  /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d] = "standby"]
  /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<worksheet, flagged>>

TearUpAndRetry(d) ==
  /\ desk[d] = "prepared"
  /\ flagged # d
  /\ worksheet[d] # drawn
  /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d] = "standby"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drawn, worksheet, flagged, posted>>

Drain ==
  /\ drawn > 0
  /\ drawn' = drawn - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<worksheet, desk, flagged, posted>>

RaiseFlag(d) ==
  /\ flagged = NoDesk
  /\ desk[d] = "prepared"
  /\ flagged' = d
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drawn, worksheet, desk, posted>>

\* The privileged push ignores the stale worksheet and reads the live figure,
\* but it is still refused if the leg would break the ceiling.
SupervisorPush(d) ==
  /\ flagged = d
  /\ desk[d] = "prepared"
  /\ drawn + LegSize <= Ceiling
  /\ drawn' = drawn + LegSize
  /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d] = "standby"]
  /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
  /\ flagged' = NoDesk
  /\ UNCHANGED worksheet

SupervisorPushAny == \E d \in Desks : SupervisorPush(d)

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Desks : PrepareLeg(d)
  \/ \E d \in Desks : PushThrough(d)
  \/ \E d \in Desks : TearUpAndRetry(d)
  \/ Drain
  \/ \E d \in Desks : RaiseFlag(d)
  \/ SupervisorPushAny

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(Drain)
  /\ SF_vars(SupervisorPushAny)

\* The ceiling holds, and it holds because no worksheet was ever taken
\* without room for the leg it will carry.
CeilingHolds ==
  /\ drawn <= Ceiling
  /\ \A d \in Desks : desk[d] = "prepared" => worksheet[d] + LegSize <= Ceiling

\* A flagged desk is out of the optimistic race and the supervisor lands it.
FlaggedDeskGetsPosted ==
  \A d \in Desks : (flagged = d) ~> (posted[d] = TRUE)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Desks = {d1, d2}
    Ceiling = 2
    LegSize = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CeilingHolds

PROPERTY FlaggedDeskGetsPosted
nl:
A clearing bank runs its interbank settlement batch against a shared intraday credit line. The credit line has a hard drawn-down ceiling: the amount drawn at any instant must never exceed it, because an overdrawn line stops the whole batch. Several member desks push settlement legs against the same line, and there is no lock on the line at all; the desks work optimistically.

A desk that is standing by may prepare a leg. Preparing reads the currently drawn amount off the line and copies it into the desk's own worksheet, and a desk is only allowed to prepare a leg if the amount it just read leaves room for a leg under the ceiling. The desk now holds a snapshot that may go stale at any moment, because other desks and the drain both move the real drawn amount.

A prepared desk may push its leg through only if its worksheet snapshot still matches the line's live drawn amount; that comparison is the whole of the optimistic scheme. On success the drawn amount goes up by one leg and the desk records its leg as posted. If the desk finds that its snapshot no longer matches the live figure, it tears the worksheet up and goes back to standing by, which is the retry. Separately, settlement traffic drains the line: whenever the drawn amount is above zero it can fall by one.

The batch supervisor holds a privileged override. The supervisor may flag one prepared desk at a time, and a flagged desk is taken out of the ordinary optimistic scheme entirely: it may no longer push through on a snapshot match and may no longer tear up its worksheet and retry. Instead the supervisor pushes the flagged desk's leg through directly, reading the live drawn amount rather than the stale worksheet, and it still refuses to push if the leg would break the ceiling. A supervisor push posts the leg and clears the flag.

The full action set is: prepare a leg at a standing-by desk when the freshly read drawn amount leaves room under the ceiling, push a prepared leg through when the worksheet snapshot still matches the live drawn amount, tear up a stale worksheet and go back to standing by, drain one leg's worth off the line, flag a prepared desk for the supervisor override, and have the supervisor push a flagged desk's leg through against the live drawn amount.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The drawn amount on the credit line never exceeds the ceiling, and every prepared desk's worksheet snapshot was itself checked to leave room for a leg under the ceiling, which is what makes an optimistic push safe.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every desk that the supervisor flags for the override eventually has its leg posted.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m6p6t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Fridges, Techs, ShiftEnd, LeaseSpan

Ticks == 0 .. ShiftEnd
NoTech == "unleased"
Commands == [fridge : Fridges, tech : Techs, stamp : Ticks]

VARIABLES clock, holder, deadline, inFlight, openBy, openStamp
vars == <<clock, holder, deadline, inFlight, openBy, openStamp>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in Ticks
  /\ holder \in [Fridges -> Techs \cup {NoTech}]
  /\ deadline \in [Fridges -> Ticks]
  /\ inFlight \in SUBSET Commands
  /\ openBy \in [Fridges -> Techs \cup {NoTech}]
  /\ openStamp \in [Fridges -> Ticks]

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ holder = [f \in Fridges |-> NoTech]
  /\ deadline = [f \in Fridges |-> 0]
  /\ inFlight = {}
  /\ openBy = [f \in Fridges |-> NoTech]
  /\ openStamp = [f \in Fridges |-> 0]

GrantLease(f, t) ==
  /\ holder[f] = NoTech
  /\ openBy[f] = NoTech
  /\ clock + LeaseSpan <= ShiftEnd
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![f] = t]
  /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![f] = clock + LeaseSpan]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, inFlight, openBy, openStamp>>

\* Commands sit in an unordered in-flight set, each carrying the lease
\* deadline that was live when it was issued.
IssueOpen(f, t) ==
  /\ holder[f] = t
  /\ clock < deadline[f]
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \cup
       {[fridge |-> f, tech |-> t, stamp |-> deadline[f]]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline, openBy, openStamp>>

Authorised(m) ==
  /\ openBy[m.fridge] = NoTech
  /\ holder[m.fridge] = m.tech
  /\ deadline[m.fridge] = m.stamp
  /\ clock < m.stamp

DeliverAccept(m) ==
  /\ m \in inFlight
  /\ Authorised(m)
  /\ openBy' = [openBy EXCEPT ![m.fridge] = m.tech]
  /\ openStamp' = [openStamp EXCEPT ![m.fridge] = m.stamp]
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline>>

DeliverDiscard(m) ==
  /\ m \in inFlight
  /\ ~Authorised(m)
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline, openBy, openStamp>>

ShutFridge(f) ==
  /\ openBy[f] # NoTech
  /\ openBy' = [openBy EXCEPT ![f] = NoTech]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline, inFlight, openStamp>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < ShiftEnd
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, deadline, inFlight, openBy, openStamp>>

\* A lease is never torn down under an open door.
TearDownLease(f) ==
  /\ holder[f] # NoTech
  /\ clock >= deadline[f]
  /\ openBy[f] = NoTech
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![f] = NoTech]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, deadline, inFlight, openBy, openStamp>>

\* When the shift is over and the floor is completely quiet, the clock is
\* reset and a fresh shift begins.
StartNewShift ==
  /\ clock = ShiftEnd
  /\ inFlight = {}
  /\ \A f \in Fridges : holder[f] = NoTech /\ openBy[f] = NoTech
  /\ clock' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, deadline, inFlight, openBy, openStamp>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Fridges, t \in Techs : GrantLease(f, t)
  \/ \E f \in Fridges, t \in Techs : IssueOpen(f, t)
  \/ \E m \in Commands : DeliverAccept(m)
  \/ \E m \in Commands : DeliverDiscard(m)
  \/ \E f \in Fridges : ShutFridge(f)
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E f \in Fridges : TearDownLease(f)
  \/ StartNewShift

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* An open door is always backed by the fridge's current lease holder and by
\* a stamp that still matches the fridge's live lease deadline.
OpenDoorIsAuthorised ==
  \A f \in Fridges :
    openBy[f] # NoTech =>
      /\ holder[f] = openBy[f]
      /\ openStamp[f] = deadline[f]
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Fridges = {f1, f2}
    Techs = {t1, t2}
    ShiftEnd = 2
    LeaseSpan = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT OpenDoorIsAuthorised
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker guards each cold-storage fridge with a lease. A technician who wants to work a fridge is granted a lease on it, and the lease carries a deadline taken from the bank's shift clock at the moment of grant. Only the technician named on a fridge's live lease is authorised to have that fridge open, and only under the deadline that the lease currently carries.

Commands from technicians do not reach the fridge controllers instantly, and the bank's messaging fabric gives no ordering guarantee at all: commands sit in flight and may be delivered in any order, so a command issued early can overtake one issued later, and a command can easily arrive after the situation that justified it has gone away. Every command therefore carries a stamp: the lease deadline that was live on that fridge when the technician issued it.

A technician holding a live lease on a fridge, one whose deadline has not yet passed on the shift clock, may issue an open command, which goes into the in-flight set stamped with that deadline. When an in-flight command is delivered, the controller accepts it only if the fridge is currently shut, the command's sender is the fridge's current lease holder, the command's stamp equals the fridge's live lease deadline, and the shift clock has not yet reached that deadline. An accepted command opens the fridge and records both who opened it and the deadline stamp it came in under. A delivered command that fails any of those tests is simply discarded.

An open fridge may be shut again at any time. The shift clock ticks forward while it is below the end of the shift. A fridge's lease may be granted to a technician only when the fridge has no lease holder and is shut, and only if the new deadline still falls within the shift. A lease whose deadline the clock has reached may be torn down, but only while the fridge is shut, so a lease is never pulled out from under an open door. When the clock has reached the end of the shift, every fridge is shut and unleased and nothing is left in flight, the bank resets the clock and a fresh shift begins.

The full action set is: grant a lease on an unleased, shut fridge to a technician, issue an open command stamped with the live lease deadline, deliver an in-flight command and accept it when sender, stamp, shut state and clock all check out, deliver an in-flight command and discard it when any of those checks fails, shut an open fridge, tick the shift clock, tear down an expired lease on a shut fridge, and start a fresh shift once the floor is completely quiet at the end of the old one.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a fridge is open, the technician who opened it is that fridge's current lease holder and the deadline stamp recorded at opening is still exactly the fridge's live lease deadline, so no reordered, stale, or unauthorised command ever leaves a fridge standing open.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m5p6t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Feeders, MaxRound, MaxBudget

Rounds == 0 .. MaxRound
NoFeeder == "noproposal"

VARIABLES round, proposal, approval, onRoster, supply, budget
vars == <<round, proposal, approval, onRoster, supply, budget>>

\* An approval is only worth anything if the node is on the live roster and
\* the approval was recorded against the round that is open now.
FreshBackers == {n \in Nodes : onRoster[n] /\ approval[n] = round}
OffSupplyCount == Cardinality({f \in Feeders : supply[f] # "live"})

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in Rounds
  /\ proposal \in Feeders \cup {NoFeeder}
  /\ approval \in [Nodes -> Rounds]
  /\ onRoster \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ supply \in [Feeders -> {"live", "shedding", "off"}]
  /\ budget \in 0 .. MaxBudget

Init ==
  /\ round = 0
  /\ proposal = NoFeeder
  /\ approval = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
  /\ onRoster = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
  /\ supply = [f \in Feeders |-> "live"]
  /\ budget = MaxBudget

OpenProposal(f) ==
  /\ proposal = NoFeeder
  /\ supply[f] = "live"
  /\ round < MaxRound
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ proposal' = f
  /\ UNCHANGED <<approval, onRoster, supply, budget>>

RecordApproval(n) ==
  /\ onRoster[n]
  /\ proposal # NoFeeder
  /\ approval[n] # round
  /\ approval' = [approval EXCEPT ![n] = round]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, proposal, onRoster, supply, budget>>

BeginShed(f) ==
  /\ proposal = f
  /\ supply[f] = "live"
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(FreshBackers) > Cardinality(Nodes)
  /\ OffSupplyCount < budget
  /\ supply' = [supply EXCEPT ![f] = "shedding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, proposal, approval, onRoster, budget>>

ConfirmOff(f) ==
  /\ supply[f] = "shedding"
  /\ supply' = [supply EXCEPT ![f] = "off"]
  /\ proposal' = NoFeeder
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, approval, onRoster, budget>>

RestoreFeeder(f) ==
  /\ supply[f] = "off"
  /\ supply' = [supply EXCEPT ![f] = "live"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, proposal, approval, onRoster, budget>>

\* The roster may not be amended out from under a shed in progress.
AmendRoster(n) ==
  /\ \A g \in Feeders : supply[g] # "shedding"
  /\ onRoster' = [onRoster EXCEPT ![n] = ~onRoster[n]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, proposal, approval, supply, budget>>

AdjustBudget(k) ==
  /\ k # budget
  /\ budget' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, proposal, approval, onRoster, supply>>

ConfirmAny == \E f \in Feeders : ConfirmOff(f)

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : OpenProposal(f)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : RecordApproval(n)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : BeginShed(f)
  \/ ConfirmAny
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : RestoreFeeder(f)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : AmendRoster(n)
  \/ \E k \in 0 .. MaxBudget : AdjustBudget(k)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(ConfirmAny)

\* A shed in progress stands on a live-round majority of on-roster nodes.
ShedIsFreshlyAuthorised ==
  \A f \in Feeders :
    supply[f] = "shedding" =>
      /\ proposal = f
      /\ 2 * Cardinality({n \in Nodes : onRoster[n] /\ approval[n] = round})
           > Cardinality(Nodes)

\* Nothing is left half-shed: the shedder always finishes what it starts.
BegunShedCompletes ==
  \A f \in Feeders : (supply[f] = "shedding") ~> (supply[f] = "off")
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
    Feeders = {x1, x2}
    MaxRound = 2
    MaxBudget = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ShedIsFreshlyAuthorised

PROPERTY BegunShedCompletes
nl:
A power-grid operator runs an automatic load shedder over a set of feeders. Taking a feeder off supply is a serious act, so it is never done on one controller's say-so: each shedding decision must be carried by a quorum of the region's control nodes, and the operator cares very much that the approvals counted are both from nodes that are actually on the live control roster and from the round of deliberation that is currently open.

Deliberation is organised in numbered rounds. Opening a proposal to shed a particular feeder bumps the round number and names that feeder as the live proposal; only one proposal is open at a time. A control node that is on the live roster may approve the open proposal, and its approval is recorded against the round number that was live when it approved. Approvals are never wiped: a node's recorded approval simply becomes stale the moment the round moves on, and a stale approval carries no weight at all in a later round.

The grid also carries a shedding budget, which is the number of feeders the operator is willing to have off supply at once, and that budget is adjusted at runtime as demand and reserve margin change. The shedder begins taking the proposed feeder off supply only when a strict majority of the on-roster control nodes have approvals recorded against the currently live round and the number of feeders already off supply is below the live budget. A feeder that is being taken off supply is then confirmed off, which also closes the proposal. A feeder that is off supply may later be restored to service.

The control roster itself changes: a node can be taken off the roster or put back on it. That amendment is only permitted while no feeder is actually mid-shed, so the quorum that a shed is standing on can never be dissolved underneath it.

The full action set is: open a proposal to shed a live feeder, which bumps the deliberation round; record an on-roster node's approval against the live round; begin taking the proposed feeder off supply when a majority of live-round approvals is in hand and the budget has room; confirm a mid-shed feeder as off supply and close the proposal; restore an off-supply feeder to service; amend the control roster while nothing is mid-shed; and adjust the shedding budget at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any feeder that is being taken off supply is the currently open proposal and is backed by approvals from a strict majority of the control nodes that are both on the live roster and recorded against the currently live deliberation round, so no off-roster node and no stale approval from an earlier round can ever carry a shed.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every feeder that the shedder has begun taking off supply is eventually confirmed as off supply.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m6p4t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Bays, Gangs, ShiftLength, LeaseSpan, MinRating, MaxRating

Ticks == 0 .. ShiftLength
NoGang == "unleased"
Ratings == MinRating .. MaxRating

VARIABLES yardClock, leaseOf, deadline, reserved, stacked, rating
vars == <<yardClock, leaseOf, deadline, reserved, stacked, rating>>

\* What a bay is carrying: boxes on the ground plus unfilled reservations.
Carried(b) == stacked[b] + reserved[b]

TypeOK ==
  /\ yardClock \in Ticks
  /\ leaseOf \in [Bays -> Gangs \cup {NoGang}]
  /\ deadline \in [Bays -> Ticks]
  /\ reserved \in [Bays -> 0 .. MaxRating]
  /\ stacked \in [Bays -> 0 .. MaxRating]
  /\ rating \in [Bays -> Ratings]

Init ==
  /\ yardClock = 0
  /\ leaseOf = [b \in Bays |-> NoGang]
  /\ deadline = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
  /\ reserved = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
  /\ stacked = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
  /\ rating = [b \in Bays |-> MaxRating]

TakeLease(b, g, k) ==
  /\ leaseOf[b] = NoGang
  /\ yardClock + LeaseSpan <= ShiftLength
  /\ stacked[b] + k <= rating[b]
  /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![b] = g]
  /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![b] = yardClock + LeaseSpan]
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![b] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardClock, stacked, rating>>

StackBox(b) ==
  /\ leaseOf[b] # NoGang
  /\ yardClock < deadline[b]
  /\ reserved[b] > 0
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![b] = reserved[b] - 1]
  /\ stacked' = [stacked EXCEPT ![b] = stacked[b] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardClock, leaseOf, deadline, rating>>

\* Handing a lease back drops every reservation it was holding.
HandBack(b) ==
  /\ leaseOf[b] # NoGang
  /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![b] = NoGang]
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardClock, deadline, stacked, rating>>

TearDownExpired(b) ==
  /\ leaseOf[b] # NoGang
  /\ yardClock >= deadline[b]
  /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![b] = NoGang]
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardClock, deadline, stacked, rating>>

LiftOut(b) ==
  /\ stacked[b] > 0
  /\ stacked' = [stacked EXCEPT ![b] = stacked[b] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardClock, leaseOf, deadline, reserved, rating>>

TickClock ==
  /\ yardClock < ShiftLength
  /\ yardClock' = yardClock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOf, deadline, reserved, stacked, rating>>

\* A re-rating may go up or down but never below what the bay carries now.
Rerate(b, r) ==
  /\ r # rating[b]
  /\ r >= Carried(b)
  /\ rating' = [rating EXCEPT ![b] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardClock, leaseOf, deadline, reserved, stacked>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bays, g \in Gangs, k \in 1 .. MaxRating : TakeLease(b, g, k)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : StackBox(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : HandBack(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : TearDownExpired(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : LiftOut(b)
  \/ TickClock
  \/ \E b \in Bays, r \in Ratings : Rerate(b, r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The rating is charged against stacked boxes and live reservations alike,
\* and an unleased bay never carries a reservation.
RatingNeverExceeded ==
  \A b \in Bays :
    /\ stacked[b] + reserved[b] <= rating[b]
    /\ leaseOf[b] = NoGang => reserved[b] = 0
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bays = {b1, b2}
    Gangs = {g1, g2}
    ShiftLength = 2
    LeaseSpan = 1
    MinRating = 1
    MaxRating = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT RatingNeverExceeded
nl:
A container-ship crane yard stacks boxes into ground bays. Every bay carries a rated ground allowance: the number of boxes actually stacked in it plus the number of ground slots that a stevedore gang has reserved but not yet filled must never exceed that rating. Going over the rating means boxes end up on the roadway.

Ground is handed out to gangs as timed leases. A gang takes a lease on a bay that currently has no lease on it, reserving a number of ground slots at the moment of the grant; the reservation is only allowed if the boxes already stacked plus the slots being reserved stay within the bay's current rating. The lease carries a deadline taken from the yard clock, and the yard clock ticks forward through the shift.

A gang holding a lease whose deadline has not yet passed may stack one box into the bay, which turns one of its reserved slots into an occupied slot. A gang may give a lease back at any time, and the yard may tear down a lease whose deadline the clock has reached. Either way the lease goes and all of that bay's outstanding reservations go with it, so unfilled reservations never linger as phantom charges against the rating. Boxes are also lifted back out of bays for loading, which frees an occupied slot outright.

Bay ratings are not fixed for the shift. The yard re-rates a bay whenever ground conditions change, and a re-rating may be up or down, but the yard refuses any new rating that would fall below what the bay is already carrying: the boxes stacked plus the slots still reserved. A re-rating is a paperwork change and must never leave a bay instantly over its allowance.

The full action set is: take a lease on an unleased bay and reserve ground slots within the bay's rating, stack a box into a leased bay against a live deadline by consuming one reserved slot, hand a lease back and drop its reservations, tear down a lease whose deadline has passed and drop its reservations, lift a stacked box back out of a bay, tick the yard clock, and re-rate a bay to any allowance that still covers what it is carrying.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every bay, the boxes stacked in it plus the ground slots still reserved against it never exceed that bay's current rating, and a bay with no lease on it carries no reservations at all.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m4p0t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Pharmacists, QueueLimit

NoOne == "trayfree"

VARIABLES queued, holdOff, trayHolder, pending, busyWith
vars == <<queued, holdOff, trayHolder, pending, busyWith>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ queued \in 0 .. QueueLimit
  /\ holdOff \in BOOLEAN
  /\ trayHolder \in Pharmacists \cup {NoOne}
  /\ pending \in [Pharmacists -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ busyWith \in [Pharmacists -> {"free", "asked", "counting"}]

Init ==
  /\ queued = 0
  /\ holdOff = FALSE
  /\ trayHolder = NoOne
  /\ pending = [p \in Pharmacists |-> FALSE]
  /\ busyWith = [p \in Pharmacists |-> "free"]

TakeIntake ==
  /\ ~holdOff
  /\ queued < QueueLimit
  /\ queued' = queued + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holdOff, trayHolder, pending, busyWith>>

RaiseHoldOff ==
  /\ ~holdOff
  /\ queued >= QueueLimit
  /\ holdOff' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, trayHolder, pending, busyWith>>

DropHoldOff ==
  /\ holdOff
  /\ queued < QueueLimit
  /\ holdOff' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, trayHolder, pending, busyWith>>

\* Requests land in an unordered inbox; nothing records who asked first.
SendRequest(p) ==
  /\ busyWith[p] = "free"
  /\ queued > 0
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ busyWith' = [busyWith EXCEPT ![p] = "asked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, holdOff, trayHolder>>

\* The dispenser serves any outstanding request, in any order it pleases,
\* and the grant consumes that request.
GrantTray(p) ==
  /\ trayHolder = NoOne
  /\ pending[p]
  /\ trayHolder' = p
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ busyWith' = [busyWith EXCEPT ![p] = "counting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, holdOff>>

FinishCount(p) ==
  /\ trayHolder = p
  /\ trayHolder' = NoOne
  /\ busyWith' = [busyWith EXCEPT ![p] = "free"]
  /\ queued' = queued - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holdOff, pending>>

RequestAny == \E p \in Pharmacists : SendRequest(p)
GrantAny == \E p \in Pharmacists : GrantTray(p)
FinishAny == \E p \in Pharmacists : FinishCount(p)

Next ==
  \/ TakeIntake
  \/ RaiseHoldOff
  \/ DropHoldOff
  \/ RequestAny
  \/ GrantAny
  \/ FinishAny

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(RequestAny)
  /\ WF_vars(GrantAny)
  /\ WF_vars(FinishAny)
  /\ WF_vars(DropHoldOff)

\* Counting is done by the recorded tray holder, whose request the dispenser
\* has already consumed out of the inbox.
TrayHeldByCounter ==
  \A p \in Pharmacists :
    busyWith[p] = "counting" =>
      /\ trayHolder = p
      /\ ~pending[p]

\* Backpressure never latches: the queue always drains far enough to clear it.
HoldOffAlwaysClears == holdOff ~> ~holdOff
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Pharmacists = {ph1, ph2}
    QueueLimit = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT TrayHeldByCounter

PROPERTY HoldOffAlwaysClears
nl:
A hospital pharmacy runs an automated prescription dispenser. Prescriptions arriving from the wards land on a bounded fill queue, and the counting tray in the middle of the dispenser is a critical resource: exactly one pharmacist may have the tray at a time, because two people counting into the same tray is how the wrong tablets end up in the wrong bottle.

Intake puts one more prescription on the fill queue, but only while the queue is below its length limit and the dispenser is not signalling backpressure. Once the queue has reached its limit the dispenser raises a backpressure signal, which stops intake outright; once the queue has fallen back below the limit the signal is dropped again.

A pharmacist who is free and can see work on the queue sends a request for the tray. Requests travel over the pharmacy's paging fabric, which gives no ordering guarantee whatsoever: outstanding requests simply sit in the dispenser's inbox, and the dispenser hands the tray to any pharmacist whose request is outstanding, in whatever order it likes, so a request sent first may well be served last. Granting the tray consumes that pharmacist's outstanding request and puts the pharmacist into the counting state. When the count is done the pharmacist gives the tray back, goes free again, and one prescription comes off the fill queue.

The full action set is: take one prescription onto the fill queue while there is room and no backpressure, raise the backpressure signal once the queue is at its limit, drop the backpressure signal once the queue is under its limit, send a tray request from a free pharmacist while there is work queued, grant the tray to any pharmacist with an outstanding request and consume that request, and finish counting, hand the tray back and take one prescription off the queue.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any pharmacist who is counting into the tray is the pharmacist the dispenser currently records as holding it and has no request still sitting outstanding in the inbox, so the tray is never being counted into by two pharmacists at once and never on the strength of a request the dispenser has not consumed.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the dispenser raises the backpressure signal, the signal is eventually dropped again.
