---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m3p5t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, RegistrarNodes, MaxTerm, MinSeats, MaxSeats

Terms == 0 .. MaxTerm

VARIABLES term, believesLeads, stage, ledger, seatCap, seatsUsed
vars == <<term, believesLeads, stage, ledger, seatCap, seatsUsed>>

\* A node may act only while the term it thinks it leads is the live term.
IsLive(n) == believesLeads[n] = term

WrittenFor(s) == Cardinality({i \in 1 .. Len(ledger) : ledger[i] = s})

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in Terms
  /\ believesLeads \in [RegistrarNodes -> Terms]
  /\ stage \in [Students -> {"applied", "approved", "committed"}]
  /\ seatCap \in MinSeats .. MaxSeats
  /\ seatsUsed \in 0 .. MaxSeats

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ believesLeads = [n \in RegistrarNodes |-> 0]
  /\ stage = [s \in Students |-> "applied"]
  /\ ledger = <<>>
  /\ seatCap = MaxSeats
  /\ seatsUsed = 0

\* Failover: an election bumps the live term and leaves every other node
\* believing it leads a term that no longer exists.
ElectLeader(n) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ believesLeads' = [believesLeads EXCEPT ![n] = term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, ledger, seatCap, seatsUsed>>

ApproveStudent(n, s) ==
  /\ IsLive(n)
  /\ stage[s] = "applied"
  /\ seatsUsed < seatCap
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "approved"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believesLeads, ledger, seatCap, seatsUsed>>

\* The irreversible step: one append to the transcript ledger.
CommitEnrolment(n, s) ==
  /\ IsLive(n)
  /\ stage[s] = "approved"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "committed"]
  /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, s)
  /\ seatsUsed' = seatsUsed + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believesLeads, seatCap>>

WithdrawApproval(n, s) ==
  /\ IsLive(n)
  /\ stage[s] = "approved"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "applied"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believesLeads, ledger, seatCap, seatsUsed>>

\* A committed student may later drop the course: the seat comes back but
\* the transcript entry it produced is permanent.
ReleaseSeat ==
  /\ seatsUsed > 0
  /\ seatsUsed' = seatsUsed - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believesLeads, stage, ledger, seatCap>>

Rerate(k) ==
  /\ k # seatCap
  /\ k >= seatsUsed
  /\ seatCap' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believesLeads, stage, ledger, seatsUsed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in RegistrarNodes : ElectLeader(n)
  \/ \E n \in RegistrarNodes, s \in Students : ApproveStudent(n, s)
  \/ \E n \in RegistrarNodes, s \in Students : CommitEnrolment(n, s)
  \/ \E n \in RegistrarNodes, s \in Students : WithdrawApproval(n, s)
  \/ ReleaseSeat
  \/ \E k \in MinSeats .. MaxSeats : Rerate(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The ledger and the student's own record agree exactly, so the append-only
\* enrolment write lands once for a committed student and never otherwise.
LedgerMatchesStage ==
  \A s \in Students :
    WrittenFor(s) = (IF stage[s] = "committed" THEN 1 ELSE 0)
=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Students = {s1, s2}
    RegistrarNodes = {n1, n2}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MinSeats = 1
    MaxSeats = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT LedgerMatchesStage
nl:
A university course-registration system is served by a small cluster of registrar nodes, exactly one of which acts as the elected leader at a time. Leadership is carried by a term number: an election bumps the cluster's term and installs the electing node as leader for that new term. Nodes that were leader in an earlier term keep their old belief about which term they lead, which is exactly what makes them stale; the cluster's live term is the only one that counts, and a node may only act if the term it believes it leads is the live one. This is how the system fails over when a registrar node drops out.

The irreversible act in this system is writing a student's enrolment into the transcript ledger. The ledger is append-only, the bursar bills off it, and an enrolment written into it cannot be unwritten. It must therefore be written for a given student at most once, even across a failover in which an old leader and a new leader might both believe they are in charge.

A student begins as applied. The live leader may approve an applied student, provided the course's seat count in use is still below the seat capacity. The live leader may commit an approved student, which writes that student into the transcript ledger, marks the student committed and takes up one seat. The live leader may also withdraw an approval, putting the student back to applied without touching the ledger. A committed student may afterwards drop the course, which hands the seat back to the pool while leaving the transcript entry exactly where it is, because that write is irreversible. Seat capacity is not fixed for the term: the registrar re-rates it at runtime, up or down, but never below the number of seats already in use.

The full action set is: elect a node as leader by bumping the cluster's term, approve an applied student while seats remain under capacity, commit an approved student by appending the enrolment to the transcript ledger and taking a seat, withdraw an approval back to applied, hand a seat back when a committed student drops the course, and re-rate the seat capacity to any figure that still covers the seats already in use.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every student, the number of times that student appears in the transcript ledger is exactly one if the student is marked committed and zero otherwise, so the irreversible enrolment write happens at most once per student no matter how leadership changes hands.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m3p5t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Controllers, BatchSize, MaxTerm

Positions == 1 .. BatchSize
Terms == 0 .. MaxTerm

VARIABLES term, believes, counter, bay, slip, waxBook
vars == <<term, believes, counter, bay, slip, waxBook>>

IsLive(c) == believes[c] = term
NextWanted == Len(waxBook) + 1

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in Terms
  /\ believes \in [Controllers -> Terms]
  /\ counter \in [Controllers -> 1 .. BatchSize + 1]
  /\ bay \in {"free", "running", "reported"}
  /\ slip \in 0 .. BatchSize

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ believes = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
  /\ counter = [c \in Controllers |-> 1]
  /\ bay = "free"
  /\ slip = 0
  /\ waxBook = <<>>

\* Failover keeps the new leader's own counter as it was; it is not
\* refreshed from the book, which is where duplicate bakes come from.
ElectLeader(c) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![c] = term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, bay, slip, waxBook>>

SendToBake(c) ==
  /\ IsLive(c)
  /\ bay = "free"
  /\ counter[c] <= BatchSize
  /\ slip' = counter[c]
  /\ bay' = "running"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, counter, waxBook>>

\* The bay is slow but never fails: a running bake always reports in the end.
BayReports ==
  /\ bay = "running"
  /\ bay' = "reported"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, counter, slip, waxBook>>

WriteIntoBook(c) ==
  /\ IsLive(c)
  /\ bay = "reported"
  /\ slip = NextWanted
  /\ waxBook' = Append(waxBook, slip)
  /\ counter' = [counter EXCEPT ![c] = slip + 1]
  /\ bay' = "free"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, slip>>

\* A rerun by a leader that was behind is thrown away rather than booked.
ThrowAwayDuplicate(c) ==
  /\ IsLive(c)
  /\ bay = "reported"
  /\ slip # NextWanted
  /\ counter' = [counter EXCEPT ![c] = NextWanted]
  /\ bay' = "free"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, slip, waxBook>>

FreshBatch ==
  /\ bay = "free"
  /\ Len(waxBook) = BatchSize
  /\ waxBook' = <<>>
  /\ counter' = [c \in Controllers |-> 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, bay, slip>>

WriteAny == \E c \in Controllers : WriteIntoBook(c)
DiscardAny == \E c \in Controllers : ThrowAwayDuplicate(c)

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : ElectLeader(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : SendToBake(c)
  \/ BayReports
  \/ WriteAny
  \/ DiscardAny
  \/ FreshBatch

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(BayReports)
  /\ WF_vars(WriteAny)
  /\ WF_vars(DiscardAny)

\* The book is the plain ascending run of conveyor positions: no gaps, and
\* above all no position booked twice.
BookIsAscendingRun ==
  \A i \in 1 .. Len(waxBook) : waxBook[i] = i

\* A slow bay still always frees up again.
StartedBakeFreesBay == (bay = "running") ~> (bay = "free")
=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    BatchSize = 2
    MaxTerm = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BookIsAscendingRun

PROPERTY StartedBakeFreesBay
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line pulls a batch of cars through a tunnel in a fixed order, position one first, then position two, and so on to the end of the batch. Near the end of the tunnel sits the hot-wax bay. Baking hot wax onto a car is irreversible: the finish cannot be stripped and re-baked, and a car that goes through the bake twice comes out scorched. The line therefore keeps a wax book, an append-only list of the conveyor positions that have actually been baked, and that book must read exactly position one, then position two, and so on with no gaps and no repeats.

The tunnel is driven by a small cluster of line controllers, one of which is the leader. Leadership is carried by a term number: an election bumps the term and installs the electing controller as leader for it, which is how the line fails over when a controller drops out. A controller may act only while the term it believes it leads is the live term. Crucially, a controller does not refresh its own idea of which position comes next when it takes over; it keeps whatever counter it was carrying, so a fresh leader can easily believe the line is further back than it really is.

The wax bay itself is slow but never fails. When the leader sends a car into the bake, the bay starts running with that conveyor position on its slip; it may take arbitrarily long, but it always eventually reports the bake as complete. Once the bay reports complete, the leader looks at the wax book. If the slip's position is exactly the next position the book is waiting for, the leader writes it into the book, advances its own counter past it and releases the bay. If the slip's position is one the book already covers, the bake was a duplicate rerun by a leader that was behind, so the result is thrown away without any write, the leader resets its counter to the position the book is actually waiting for, and the bay is released. When the whole batch has been baked and the bay is idle, the tunnel takes a fresh batch, which empties the wax book and resets every controller's counter to position one.

The full action set is: elect a controller as leader by bumping the term, send the position on the leader's counter into the wax bay when the bay is free, have the slow bay report a running bake as complete, write a completed bake into the wax book when its position is the one the book is waiting for, throw away a completed bake whose position the book already covers, and start a fresh batch once the book is full and the bay is free.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The wax book always reads as the plain ascending run of conveyor positions, entry one being position one, entry two being position two and so on, so no conveyor position is ever written into it twice and the irreversible hot-wax bake is booked at most once per car.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Any bake that the wax bay has started eventually leaves the bay free again.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m3p5t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Symbols, Engines, TapeRoom, MaxTerm

Terms == 0 .. MaxTerm
Budgets == 0 .. TapeRoom

VARIABLES term, believes, tape, tapePos, budget, matched
vars == <<term, believes, tape, tapePos, budget, matched>>

LeadsNow(e) == believes[e] = term

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in Terms
  /\ believes \in [Engines -> Terms]
  /\ tapePos \in [Symbols -> 0 .. TapeRoom]
  /\ budget \in Budgets
  /\ matched \in [Symbols -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ believes = [e \in Engines |-> 0]
  /\ tape = <<>>
  /\ tapePos = [y \in Symbols |-> 0]
  /\ budget = TapeRoom
  /\ matched = [y \in Symbols |-> FALSE]

\* Failover: an election bumps the live term and leaves earlier leaders inert.
ElectEngine(e) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![e] = term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tape, tapePos, budget, matched>>

CrossBook(e, y) ==
  /\ LeadsNow(e)
  /\ ~matched[y]
  /\ tapePos[y] = 0
  /\ matched' = [matched EXCEPT ![y] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, tape, tapePos, budget>>

BackOutMatch(e, y) ==
  /\ LeadsNow(e)
  /\ matched[y]
  /\ tapePos[y] = 0
  /\ matched' = [matched EXCEPT ![y] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, tape, tapePos, budget>>

\* The irreversible step: one append to the tape, with the tape position
\* written back against the symbol in the same instant.
PublishPrint(e, y) ==
  /\ LeadsNow(e)
  /\ matched[y]
  /\ tapePos[y] = 0
  /\ Len(tape) < budget
  /\ tape' = Append(tape, y)
  /\ tapePos' = [tapePos EXCEPT ![y] = Len(tape) + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, budget, matched>>

AdjustBudget(k) ==
  /\ k # budget
  /\ k >= Len(tape)
  /\ budget' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, tape, tapePos, matched>>

OpenNewSession ==
  /\ \A y \in Symbols : tapePos[y] # 0
  /\ tape' = <<>>
  /\ tapePos' = [y \in Symbols |-> 0]
  /\ matched' = [y \in Symbols |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, budget>>

Next ==
  \/ \E e \in Engines : ElectEngine(e)
  \/ \E e \in Engines, y \in Symbols : CrossBook(e, y)
  \/ \E e \in Engines, y \in Symbols : BackOutMatch(e, y)
  \/ \E e \in Engines, y \in Symbols : PublishPrint(e, y)
  \/ \E k \in Budgets : AdjustBudget(k)
  \/ OpenNewSession

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Tape and recorded positions are mutual inverses, which is exactly what
\* stops one symbol's irreversible print from landing on the tape twice.
TapeAndPositionsAgree ==
  /\ \A y \in Symbols : tapePos[y] # 0 => tape[tapePos[y]] = y
  /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(tape) : tapePos[tape[i]] = i
===========================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Symbols = {y1, y2}
    Engines = {e1, e2}
    TapeRoom = 2
    MaxTerm = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT TapeAndPositionsAgree
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction across a set of symbols. For each symbol the auction eventually publishes an opening print onto the official tape. Publishing an opening print is irreversible: the print is disseminated to every market data feed the instant it is written, indices and settlement prices are struck off it, and it cannot be recalled. A symbol must therefore be printed onto the tape at most once in a session.

The tape is an ordered record of the prints made this session, and alongside it the exchange keeps, for each symbol, the tape position at which that symbol's print sits, or zero if the symbol has not printed. The two records have to agree with each other in both directions: the position recorded against a symbol must genuinely hold that symbol's print, and every entry on the tape must be recorded against the symbol it names at exactly that position.

The auction is driven by a cluster of matching engines with one elected leader. Leadership is carried by a term: an election bumps the exchange's term and installs the electing engine as leader of it, which is how the auction fails over when an engine drops out. An engine may act only while the term it believes it leads is the exchange's live term, so an engine left over from an earlier term is inert.

The live leader may cross a symbol's book, marking that symbol as matched and ready to print, and may equally back a match out again while the symbol is still unprinted. The live leader publishes a matched, unprinted symbol by appending its print to the tape and recording the tape position against the symbol. The session also carries a print budget, the number of prints the exchange is prepared to disseminate in this session, and that budget is adjusted at runtime as feed load changes; the exchange refuses any new budget that is below the number of prints already on the tape, and refuses to publish once the tape has reached the budget. When every symbol has printed, the exchange opens a new session, clearing the tape, the recorded positions and the match marks.

The full action set is: elect an engine as leader by bumping the term, cross a symbol's book to mark it matched, back a match out while the symbol is still unprinted, publish a matched symbol's opening print onto the tape and record its tape position, adjust the session print budget at runtime to any figure that still covers the tape, and open a new session once every symbol has printed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The tape and the per-symbol tape positions always agree in both directions, so the position recorded against a symbol holds that symbol's print and each tape entry is recorded at exactly its own position, which means no symbol's irreversible opening print is ever written onto the tape twice.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m2p0t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, DoorHubs

Nobody == "nodriver"
NoProposal == "noproposal"

VARIABLES proposal, ballot, driver, stance, bolt
vars == <<proposal, ballot, driver, stance, bolt>>

AllIn == \A h \in DoorHubs : ballot[h] # "open"
AllYes == \A h \in DoorHubs : ballot[h] = "yes"

TypeOK ==
  /\ proposal \in Controllers \cup {NoProposal}
  /\ ballot \in [DoorHubs -> {"open", "yes", "no"}]
  /\ driver \in Controllers \cup {Nobody}
  /\ stance \in [Controllers -> {"quiet", "proposing", "driving"}]
  /\ bolt \in {"thrown", "unlocked"}

Init ==
  /\ proposal = NoProposal
  /\ ballot = [h \in DoorHubs |-> "open"]
  /\ driver = Nobody
  /\ stance = [k \in Controllers |-> "quiet"]
  /\ bolt = "thrown"

OpenProposal(k) ==
  /\ proposal = NoProposal
  /\ driver = Nobody
  /\ stance[k] = "quiet"
  /\ proposal' = k
  /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![k] = "proposing"]
  /\ ballot' = [h \in DoorHubs |-> "open"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<driver, bolt>>

\* Hubs are slow but never silent; a hub refuses while the house is open.
CastBallot(h) ==
  /\ proposal # NoProposal
  /\ ballot[h] = "open"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![h] =
        IF bolt = "thrown" THEN "yes" ELSE "no"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, driver, stance, bolt>>

CommitDrive ==
  /\ proposal # NoProposal
  /\ AllIn
  /\ AllYes
  /\ driver' = proposal
  /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![proposal] = "driving"]
  /\ proposal' = NoProposal
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, bolt>>

AbandonProposal ==
  /\ proposal # NoProposal
  /\ AllIn
  /\ ~AllYes
  /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![proposal] = "quiet"]
  /\ proposal' = NoProposal
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, driver, bolt>>

WorkBolt(k) ==
  /\ driver = k
  /\ bolt' = IF bolt = "thrown" THEN "unlocked" ELSE "thrown"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, ballot, driver, stance>>

GiveUpDrive(k) ==
  /\ driver = k
  /\ driver' = Nobody
  /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![k] = "quiet"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, ballot, bolt>>

AutoRelock ==
  /\ driver = Nobody
  /\ bolt = "unlocked"
  /\ bolt' = "thrown"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, ballot, driver, stance>>

BallotAny == \E h \in DoorHubs : CastBallot(h)
Resolve == CommitDrive \/ AbandonProposal

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Controllers : OpenProposal(k)
  \/ BallotAny
  \/ Resolve
  \/ \E k \in Controllers : WorkBolt(k)
  \/ \E k \in Controllers : GiveUpDrive(k)
  \/ AutoRelock

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(BallotAny)
  /\ WF_vars(Resolve)

\* Driving is backed by a closed proposal and a full sweep of yes ballots,
\* which is what keeps a second controller off the actuator.
DriveIsUnanimouslyHeld ==
  \A k \in Controllers :
    stance[k] = "driving" =>
      /\ driver = k
      /\ proposal = NoProposal
      /\ \A h \in DoorHubs : ballot[h] = "yes"

\* A slow hub is still a hub that answers.
OpenBallotsGetCast ==
  \A h \in DoorHubs :
    (proposal # NoProposal /\ ballot[h] = "open") ~> (ballot[h] # "open")
===========================================================================
nl:
A smart-home installation has several controllers, a phone app, a wall panel and a voice assistant, and a network of door hubs. The front-door deadbolt actuator is a critical resource: exactly one controller may hold the drive on it at a time, because two controllers driving the same motor at once is how a door ends up jammed half-thrown.

The drive is handed out by a two-phase agreement across all the door hubs. A quiet controller may open a proposal for the drive, but only when nobody currently holds the drive and no other proposal is open; opening a proposal clears every hub's ballot back to open. Each door hub then casts its ballot on the proposal. A hub votes yes if the deadbolt is currently thrown, and votes no if the deadbolt is standing unlocked, because a hub will not hand exclusive motor control to a controller while the house is open. The hubs are slow but they never fail: a hub may take arbitrarily long to answer, but it always answers in the end, which is why the agreement simply waits for every ballot rather than timing hubs out.

Once every hub has balloted, the agreement resolves. If every ballot is yes, the drive commits to the proposing controller, which becomes the driver, and the proposal closes. If any ballot is no, the proposal is abandoned, the controller goes quiet again and nothing is handed out. A controller holding the drive may work the deadbolt, throwing it from locked to unlocked or back, and may give the drive up at any time and go quiet. Separately, when nobody holds the drive and the deadbolt is standing unlocked, the house auto-relocks it.

The full action set is: open a proposal for the drive from a quiet controller while the drive is free and no proposal is open, cast a door hub's ballot on the open proposal according to the deadbolt's current state, commit the drive to the proposer once every ballot is yes, abandon the proposal once every ballot is in and some ballot is no, work the deadbolt as the current driver, give the drive up and go quiet, and auto-relock an unlocked deadbolt while the drive is free.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A controller that holds the drive is the one the network records as driver, has no proposal still open against it, and holds a full set of yes ballots from every door hub, so two controllers can never be driving the deadbolt actuator at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every door hub with an open ballot against an open proposal eventually casts that ballot.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m5p0t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Supervisors, MaxFleet

Unspent == "unspent"
LandingFree == "landingfree"

VARIABLES pledge, landing, carPhase, inService, fleetAllowance
vars == <<pledge, landing, carPhase, inService, fleetAllowance>>

PledgedTo(c) == {d \in Supervisors : pledge[d] = c}
Majority(c) == 2 * Cardinality(PledgedTo(c)) > Cardinality(Supervisors)
CarsInService == Cardinality({c \in Cars : inService[c]})

TypeOK ==
  /\ pledge \in [Supervisors -> Cars \cup {Unspent}]
  /\ landing \in Cars \cup {LandingFree}
  /\ carPhase \in [Cars -> {"parked", "seeking", "berthed"}]
  /\ inService \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ fleetAllowance \in 0 .. MaxFleet

Init ==
  /\ pledge = [d \in Supervisors |-> Unspent]
  /\ landing = LandingFree
  /\ carPhase = [c \in Cars |-> "parked"]
  /\ inService = [c \in Cars |-> TRUE]
  /\ fleetAllowance = MaxFleet

StartSeeking(c) ==
  /\ inService[c]
  /\ carPhase[c] = "parked"
  /\ carPhase' = [carPhase EXCEPT ![c] = "seeking"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pledge, landing, inService, fleetAllowance>>

GivePledge(d, c) ==
  /\ pledge[d] = Unspent
  /\ carPhase[c] = "seeking"
  /\ pledge' = [pledge EXCEPT ![d] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<landing, carPhase, inService, fleetAllowance>>

\* Backing cannot be pulled out from under a car that is already berthed.
TakePledgeBack(d) ==
  /\ pledge[d] # Unspent
  /\ carPhase[pledge[d]] # "berthed"
  /\ pledge' = [pledge EXCEPT ![d] = Unspent]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<landing, carPhase, inService, fleetAllowance>>

MoveOntoLanding(c) ==
  /\ carPhase[c] = "seeking"
  /\ landing = LandingFree
  /\ inService[c]
  /\ Majority(c)
  /\ landing' = c
  /\ carPhase' = [carPhase EXCEPT ![c] = "berthed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pledge, inService, fleetAllowance>>

PullOffLanding(c) ==
  /\ carPhase[c] = "berthed"
  /\ landing' = LandingFree
  /\ carPhase' = [carPhase EXCEPT ![c] = "parked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pledge, inService, fleetAllowance>>

\* Service status only changes while a car is parked, and bringing a car up
\* has to fit inside the live fleet allowance.
ChangeService(c, s) ==
  /\ inService[c] # s
  /\ carPhase[c] = "parked"
  /\ (s => CarsInService < fleetAllowance)
  /\ inService' = [inService EXCEPT ![c] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pledge, landing, carPhase, fleetAllowance>>

AdjustAllowance(k) ==
  /\ k # fleetAllowance
  /\ k >= CarsInService
  /\ fleetAllowance' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pledge, landing, carPhase, inService>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : StartSeeking(c)
  \/ \E d \in Supervisors, c \in Cars : GivePledge(d, c)
  \/ \E d \in Supervisors : TakePledgeBack(d)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : MoveOntoLanding(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : PullOffLanding(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars, s \in BOOLEAN : ChangeService(c, s)
  \/ \E k \in 0 .. MaxFleet : AdjustAllowance(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A berthed car is the recorded occupant, carries a strict majority of the
\* single supervisor pledges, and is in service.
BerthIsMajorityBacked ==
  \A c \in Cars :
    carPhase[c] = "berthed" =>
      /\ landing = c
      /\ 2 * Cardinality({d \in Supervisors : pledge[d] = c})
           > Cardinality(Supervisors)
      /\ inService[c]
=============================================================================
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank shares one sky-lobby transfer landing between its cars. The landing is a critical resource: only one car may be standing on it at a time, because two cars berthed on the same landing would foul each other's doors and trap passengers between them.

There is no single dispatcher that owns the landing. Instead the bank's supervisory controllers vote. Each controller has exactly one pledge to give at a time. A controller with an unspent pledge may pledge it to any car that is currently seeking the landing. A controller may take its pledge back from a car, but never from a car that is actually standing on the landing, so a car's backing cannot be dismantled while it is berthed. A car may move onto the free landing only once it holds pledges from a strict majority of the controllers, and only while it is in service.

The bank also runs under a fleet allowance: the number of cars the building is willing to have in service at once. That allowance is adjusted at runtime as traffic and power budget change, and the building refuses any new allowance below the number of cars already in service. A car may be brought into service only while the cars in service are still under the allowance, and a car may be taken out of service only while it is parked, never while it is seeking or berthed.

A parked, in-service car may start seeking the landing. A car standing on the landing may pull off it and go back to parked, freeing the landing.

The full action set is: start a parked in-service car seeking the landing, pledge an unspent controller vote to a seeking car, take a controller's pledge back from a car that is not standing on the landing, move a seeking car with a majority of pledges onto the free landing, pull a berthed car off the landing back to parked, change a parked car's in-service status within the fleet allowance, and adjust the fleet allowance at runtime to any figure that still covers the cars in service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any car standing on the sky-lobby landing is the car the bank records as berthed, holds pledges from a strict majority of the supervisory controllers, and is in service, so with one pledge per controller two cars can never be berthed on the landing at once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m2p3t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS CatalogueNodes, NumSlots

Services == {"A", "B"}
Slots == 1 .. NumSlots
NoSlot == 0
Unallocated == "unallocated"

VARIABLES phase, txnSlot, ballot, shelfCard, deskRecord
vars == <<phase, txnSlot, ballot, shelfCard, deskRecord>>

AllBalloted(i) == \A n \in CatalogueNodes : ballot[n][i] # "open"
AllYes(i) == \A n \in CatalogueNodes : ballot[n][i] = "yes"

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Services -> {"idle", "voting"}]
  /\ txnSlot \in [Services -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ ballot \in [CatalogueNodes -> [Services -> {"open", "yes", "no"}]]
  /\ shelfCard \in [Slots -> Services \cup {Unallocated}]
  /\ deskRecord \in [Services -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]

Init ==
  /\ phase = [i \in Services |-> "idle"]
  /\ txnSlot = [i \in Services |-> NoSlot]
  /\ ballot = [n \in CatalogueNodes |-> [i \in Services |-> "open"]]
  /\ shelfCard = [s \in Slots |-> Unallocated]
  /\ deskRecord = [i \in Services |-> NoSlot]

\* Each service runs its own reservation, so a node holds one ballot per
\* service and the two services genuinely race for the same slot.
OpenReservation(i, s) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "idle"
  /\ deskRecord[i] = NoSlot
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "voting"]
  /\ txnSlot' = [txnSlot EXCEPT ![i] = s]
  /\ ballot' = [n \in CatalogueNodes |-> [ballot[n] EXCEPT ![i] = "open"]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfCard, deskRecord>>

CastBallot(n, i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "voting"
  /\ ballot[n][i] = "open"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![n][i] =
        IF shelfCard[txnSlot[i]] = Unallocated THEN "yes" ELSE "no"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, txnSlot, shelfCard, deskRecord>>

\* The decision re-reads the shelf, because the rival service may have taken
\* the slot after the ballots were cast.
CommitReservation(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "voting"
  /\ AllYes(i)
  /\ shelfCard[txnSlot[i]] = Unallocated
  /\ shelfCard' = [shelfCard EXCEPT ![txnSlot[i]] = i]
  /\ deskRecord' = [deskRecord EXCEPT ![i] = txnSlot[i]]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
  /\ txnSlot' = [txnSlot EXCEPT ![i] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED ballot

AbandonReservation(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "voting"
  /\ AllBalloted(i)
  /\ ~(AllYes(i) /\ shelfCard[txnSlot[i]] = Unallocated)
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
  /\ txnSlot' = [txnSlot EXCEPT ![i] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, shelfCard, deskRecord>>

CollectItem(i) ==
  /\ deskRecord[i] # NoSlot
  /\ shelfCard' = [shelfCard EXCEPT ![deskRecord[i]] = Unallocated]
  /\ deskRecord' = [deskRecord EXCEPT ![i] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, txnSlot, ballot>>

CollectA == CollectItem("A")
CollectB == CollectItem("B")

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Services, s \in Slots : OpenReservation(i, s)
  \/ \E n \in CatalogueNodes, i \in Services : CastBallot(n, i)
  \/ \E i \in Services : CommitReservation(i)
  \/ \E i \in Services : AbandonReservation(i)
  \/ CollectA
  \/ CollectB

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(CollectA)
  /\ WF_vars(CollectB)

\* Shelf cards and desk records are mutual inverses, and an occupied slot
\* still carries a full set of standing yes ballots.
HoldShelfSound ==
  /\ \A i \in Services : deskRecord[i] # NoSlot => shelfCard[deskRecord[i]] = i
  /\ \A s \in Slots : shelfCard[s] # Unallocated => deskRecord[shelfCard[s]] = s
  /\ \A s \in Slots :
       shelfCard[s] # Unallocated =>
         \A n \in CatalogueNodes : ballot[n][shelfCard[s]] = "yes"

\* Nothing sits on the hold shelf for ever.
HeldSlotIsCollected ==
  \A i \in Services : (deskRecord[i] # NoSlot) ~> (deskRecord[i] = NoSlot)
===========================================================================

CONSTANTS
    CatalogueNodes = {n1, n2}
    NumSlots = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT HoldShelfSound

PROPERTY HeldSlotIsCollected
nl:
A public library runs two independent reservation services, service A at the main desk and service B on the website, and both of them allocate out of the same shared pool of hold-shelf slots behind the pickup counter. Neither service owns a range of slots; both reach into the same pool, and both may be running a reservation at the same moment. A hold-shelf slot must never be allocated to two reservations at once, or two patrons turn up for the same shelf position.

Each service runs its own two-phase reservation against the library's catalogue nodes. A service that is idle and is not already holding a slot opens a reservation on a slot of its choosing, which clears that service's ballot at every catalogue node. Each catalogue node then votes on that service's open reservation: it votes yes if the slot named in the reservation is free according to the shelf cards, and no otherwise. The two services' ballots are independent, so a node holds one ballot per service.

Once every node has voted yes on a service's reservation and the named slot is still free at decision time, the reservation commits: a shelf card for that service goes into the slot and the service's desk record is written with the slot number. If every node has voted but the reservation cannot commit, either because some node voted no or because the slot was taken in the meantime by the other service, the reservation is abandoned and nothing is written. A service holding a slot eventually has its patron collect the item, which pulls the shelf card out of the slot and clears the service's desk record.

The full action set is: open a reservation on a slot from an idle service that holds nothing and clear that service's ballots, cast a catalogue node's ballot on a service's open reservation according to whether the named slot is free, commit a reservation whose ballots are all yes and whose slot is still free by writing both the shelf card and the desk record, abandon a fully balloted reservation that cannot commit, and collect a held item, which clears both the shelf card and the desk record.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shelf cards and the services' desk records always agree with each other in both directions, and every occupied slot is backed by a full set of standing yes ballots from every catalogue node, so the same hold-shelf slot is never allocated to both services at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: A service that is holding a hold-shelf slot eventually has that slot collected and its desk record cleared.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m2p2t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS NumStations, Relays, OpeningLoad, MaxLoad, LedgerRoom

Stations == 1 .. NumStations
NoStation == 0
NoTransfer == [src |-> NoStation, dst |-> NoStation]

VARIABLES load, credits, debits, transfer, ballot
vars == <<load, credits, debits, transfer, ballot>>

RECURSIVE SumOf(_, _)
SumOf(f, k) == IF k = 0 THEN 0 ELSE f[k] + SumOf(f, k - 1)

AllBalloted == \A r \in Relays : ballot[r] # "open"
Unanimous == \A r \in Relays : ballot[r] = "yes"

TypeOK ==
  /\ load \in [Stations -> 0 .. MaxLoad]
  /\ credits \in [Stations -> 0 .. LedgerRoom]
  /\ debits \in [Stations -> 0 .. LedgerRoom]
  /\ transfer \in [src : Stations \cup {NoStation}, dst : Stations \cup {NoStation}]
  /\ ballot \in [Relays -> {"open", "yes", "no"}]

Init ==
  /\ load = [b \in Stations |-> OpeningLoad]
  /\ credits = [b \in Stations |-> 0]
  /\ debits = [b \in Stations |-> 0]
  /\ transfer = NoTransfer
  /\ ballot = [r \in Relays |-> "open"]

\* A transfer can only be applied if both sides and both ledger columns can
\* take it; this is the guard the abandon path mirrors.
Applicable ==
  /\ load[transfer.src] > 0
  /\ load[transfer.dst] < MaxLoad
  /\ debits[transfer.src] < LedgerRoom
  /\ credits[transfer.dst] < LedgerRoom

ProposeTransfer(s, d) ==
  /\ transfer = NoTransfer
  /\ s # d
  /\ load[s] > 0
  /\ transfer' = [src |-> s, dst |-> d]
  /\ ballot' = [r \in Relays |-> "open"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, credits, debits>>

CastBallot(r) ==
  /\ transfer # NoTransfer
  /\ ballot[r] = "open"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![r] =
        IF load[transfer.dst] < MaxLoad THEN "yes" ELSE "no"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, credits, debits, transfer>>

\* One block moves and the matching debit and credit are written together.
ApplyBlock ==
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![transfer.src] = load[transfer.src] - 1,
                         ![transfer.dst] = load[transfer.dst] + 1]
  /\ debits' = [debits EXCEPT ![transfer.src] = debits[transfer.src] + 1]
  /\ credits' = [credits EXCEPT ![transfer.dst] = credits[transfer.dst] + 1]
  /\ transfer' = NoTransfer

CommitTransfer ==
  /\ transfer # NoTransfer
  /\ AllBalloted
  /\ Unanimous
  /\ Applicable
  /\ ApplyBlock
  /\ UNCHANGED ballot

AbandonTransfer ==
  /\ transfer # NoTransfer
  /\ AllBalloted
  /\ ~(Unanimous /\ Applicable)
  /\ transfer' = NoTransfer
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, credits, debits, ballot>>

\* The supervisor override skips the ballots but never skips the books.
SupervisorForce ==
  /\ transfer # NoTransfer
  /\ Applicable
  /\ ApplyBlock
  /\ UNCHANGED ballot

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Stations, d \in Stations : ProposeTransfer(s, d)
  \/ \E r \in Relays : CastBallot(r)
  \/ CommitTransfer
  \/ AbandonTransfer
  \/ SupervisorForce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Double entry: every station's live load reconciles against its own ledger
\* columns, and the region's credits and debits match exactly.
GridBooksBalance ==
  /\ \A b \in Stations : load[b] = OpeningLoad + credits[b] - debits[b]
  /\ SumOf(credits, NumStations) = SumOf(debits, NumStations)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumStations = 2
    Relays = {r1, r2}
    OpeningLoad = 1
    MaxLoad = 2
    LedgerRoom = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT GridBooksBalance
nl:
A regional power-grid load shedder moves whole blocks of demand between substations. The megawatt blocks on the network are a fixed inventory for the shift: a block moved off one substation must land on another, and the control room keeps a double-entry book so that no block can be conjured into existence or quietly lost when a transfer goes wrong.

The book works like any double-entry ledger. Each substation has an opening figure for the shift, a running credit total for blocks that have landed on it, and a running debit total for blocks that have left it. The control room's rule is that each substation's live load must always equal its opening figure plus its credits minus its debits, and that the credits across the whole region must always equal the debits across the whole region.

A transfer is agreed by two-phase commit across the grid's protection relays. The control room proposes moving one block from a source substation that has a block to give to a destination substation that has headroom, which clears every relay's ballot. Each relay then votes: yes if the destination still has headroom, no otherwise. Once every relay has voted, the transfer commits if the ballots are unanimous, the source still has a block, the destination still has headroom and neither substation's ledger column has run out of room; committing takes one block off the source, puts one on the destination, and writes one debit and one credit in the same stroke. If a fully balloted transfer cannot be applied for any of those reasons it is abandoned outright, and no ledger line is written.

The control room supervisor also holds a privileged override. The supervisor may force a proposed transfer through without waiting for the relays to agree at all, which is used when a cascade is developing and there is no time to poll. The override skips the ballots entirely but it does not skip the books: it still checks that the source has a block, that the destination has headroom and that the ledger columns have room, and it still writes the matching debit and credit.

The full action set is: propose a one-block transfer between substations and clear the relay ballots, cast a relay's ballot on the open transfer according to the destination's headroom, commit a unanimously balloted transfer that can still be applied by writing the matching debit and credit, abandon a fully balloted transfer that cannot be applied, and have the supervisor force a proposed transfer through on the override while still writing both ledger lines.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every substation's live load always equals its opening figure plus its credits minus its debits, and the region's total credits always equal its total debits, so no megawatt block is ever created or destroyed by a transfer, an abandonment or a supervisor override.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m8p5t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Scripts, NumDrawers, ColdUpTo

Robots == {"A", "B"}
Drawers == 1 .. NumDrawers
Zones == {"cold", "ambient"}
FreeLock == "unlocked"
NoScript == "emptyhands"

ZoneOf(d) == IF d <= ColdUpTo THEN "cold" ELSE "ambient"

VARIABLES zoneLock, drawerLock, carrying, sealed, tamperTag, inPool
vars == <<zoneLock, drawerLock, carrying, sealed, tamperTag, inPool>>

TagsFor(p) == Cardinality({d \in Drawers : tamperTag[d] = p})

TypeOK ==
  /\ zoneLock \in [Zones -> Robots \cup {FreeLock}]
  /\ drawerLock \in [Drawers -> Robots \cup {FreeLock}]
  /\ carrying \in [Robots -> Scripts \cup {NoScript}]
  /\ sealed \in [Scripts -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ tamperTag \in [Drawers -> Scripts \cup {NoScript}]
  /\ inPool \in [Scripts -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ zoneLock = [z \in Zones |-> FreeLock]
  /\ drawerLock = [d \in Drawers |-> FreeLock]
  /\ carrying = [rb \in Robots |-> NoScript]
  /\ sealed = [p \in Scripts |-> FALSE]
  /\ tamperTag = [d \in Drawers |-> NoScript]
  /\ inPool = [p \in Scripts |-> TRUE]

PickUp(rb, p) ==
  /\ carrying[rb] = NoScript
  /\ inPool[p]
  /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![rb] = p]
  /\ inPool' = [inPool EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, drawerLock, sealed, tamperTag>>

TakeZoneLock(rb, z) ==
  /\ carrying[rb] # NoScript
  /\ zoneLock[z] = FreeLock
  /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![z] = rb]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drawerLock, carrying, sealed, tamperTag, inPool>>

\* The fine lock is only reachable through the coarse lock on its zone.
TakeDrawerLock(rb, d) ==
  /\ zoneLock[ZoneOf(d)] = rb
  /\ drawerLock[d] = FreeLock
  /\ drawerLock' = [drawerLock EXCEPT ![d] = rb]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, carrying, sealed, tamperTag, inPool>>

\* The irreversible step: one foil seal, one tamper tag left behind.
SealInto(rb, d) ==
  /\ carrying[rb] # NoScript
  /\ zoneLock[ZoneOf(d)] = rb
  /\ drawerLock[d] = rb
  /\ tamperTag[d] = NoScript
  /\ sealed' = [sealed EXCEPT ![carrying[rb]] = TRUE]
  /\ tamperTag' = [tamperTag EXCEPT ![d] = carrying[rb]]
  /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![rb] = NoScript]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, drawerLock, inPool>>

\* Locks only go back when the robot's hands are empty.
GiveBackLocks(rb) ==
  /\ carrying[rb] = NoScript
  /\ (\E z \in Zones : zoneLock[z] = rb) \/ (\E d \in Drawers : drawerLock[d] = rb)
  /\ zoneLock' = [z \in Zones |-> IF zoneLock[z] = rb THEN FreeLock ELSE zoneLock[z]]
  /\ drawerLock' = [d \in Drawers |-> IF drawerLock[d] = rb THEN FreeLock ELSE drawerLock[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<carrying, sealed, tamperTag, inPool>>

EmptyCabinet ==
  /\ \A d \in Drawers : tamperTag[d] # NoScript
  /\ (\A z \in Zones : zoneLock[z] = FreeLock)
  /\ (\A d \in Drawers : drawerLock[d] = FreeLock) /\ (\A rb \in Robots : carrying[rb] = NoScript)
  /\ tamperTag' = [d \in Drawers |-> NoScript]
  /\ sealed' = [p \in Scripts |-> FALSE]
  /\ inPool' = [p \in Scripts |-> TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, drawerLock, carrying>>

SealByA == \E d \in Drawers : SealInto("A", d)
SealByB == \E d \in Drawers : SealInto("B", d)

Next ==
  \/ \E rb \in Robots, p \in Scripts : PickUp(rb, p)
  \/ \E rb \in Robots, z \in Zones : TakeZoneLock(rb, z)
  \/ \E rb \in Robots, d \in Drawers : TakeDrawerLock(rb, d)
  \/ SealByA
  \/ SealByB
  \/ \E rb \in Robots : GiveBackLocks(rb)
  \/ EmptyCabinet

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(SealByA)
  /\ WF_vars(SealByB)

\* Exactly one tamper tag exists for a sealed prescription and none for an
\* unsealed one, so the single-use foil is spent at most once per script.
SealAppliedAtMostOnce ==
  \A p \in Scripts : TagsFor(p) = (IF sealed[p] THEN 1 ELSE 0)

\* A robot holding both locks over a clean drawer always gets to put its
\* dose away, so it never stands there loaded for ever.
LoadedRobotSealsThrough ==
  \A rb \in Robots :
    ( carrying[rb] # NoScript /\ \E d \in Drawers :
        zoneLock[ZoneOf(d)] = rb /\ drawerLock[d] = rb /\ tamperTag[d] = NoScript )
      ~> (carrying[rb] = NoScript)
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Scripts = {p1, p2}
    NumDrawers = 2
    ColdUpTo = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SealAppliedAtMostOnce

PROPERTY LoadedRobotSealsThrough
nl:
A hospital pharmacy runs two independent compounding robots, robot A and robot B, and both of them draw work from the same shared pool of prescriptions. Neither robot owns a set of prescriptions; whichever robot picks one up out of the pool carries it.

The finished dose is put away in a numbered drawer of the compounding cabinet, and the drawers are grouped into two temperature zones. Applying the tamper seal to a dose is irreversible: the seal is a single-use foil that carries the batch record, it cannot be lifted and re-applied, and a dose that gets sealed twice has to be destroyed. Every seal that is applied leaves its tamper tag in the drawer it was applied in, so the cabinet's drawers are the physical record of which prescriptions have been sealed.

Access to the cabinet is layered. A robot carrying a prescription must first take the coarse lock on a temperature zone, and only while it holds a zone's coarse lock may it take the fine lock on an individual drawer inside that zone. A robot may seal its dose into a drawer only while it holds both the coarse lock on that drawer's zone and the fine lock on that drawer, and only if the drawer has no tamper tag in it yet; sealing marks the prescription sealed, leaves the tamper tag in the drawer and leaves the robot's hands empty. A robot may give back every lock it holds, but only once its hands are empty, so it never abandons a job halfway through the cabinet.

When every drawer in the cabinet holds a tamper tag, the locks are all free and neither robot is carrying anything, the cabinet is emptied for the next batch: the tamper tags come out, the prescriptions go back into the shared pool and the seal records are cleared together.

The full action set is: pick a prescription out of the shared pool with empty hands, take the coarse lock on a temperature zone while carrying a prescription, take the fine lock on a drawer inside a zone whose coarse lock is already held, seal the carried dose into a fully locked untagged drawer, give back all of a robot's locks once its hands are empty, and empty the cabinet for a new batch once every drawer is tagged and everything is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every prescription, the number of drawers holding that prescription's tamper tag is exactly one if the prescription is marked sealed and zero otherwise, so the irreversible seal is applied to a given prescription at most once even though two robots draw from the same pool.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: A robot that is carrying a prescription and already holds both the coarse lock on a zone and the fine lock on an untagged drawer in that zone eventually ends up with empty hands.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m3p4t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumCars, Dispatchers, CarRating, BankLimit, LobbyPeople, MaxTerm

Cars == 1 .. NumCars
Terms == 0 .. MaxTerm

VARIABLES term, believes, riding, committed, carUp, lobby
vars == <<term, believes, riding, committed, carUp, lobby>>

RECURSIVE SumOf(_, _)
SumOf(f, k) == IF k = 0 THEN 0 ELSE f[k] + SumOf(f, k - 1)

LeadsNow(n) == believes[n] = term
InTransit == SumOf(riding, NumCars) + SumOf(committed, NumCars)

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in Terms
  /\ believes \in [Dispatchers -> Terms]
  /\ riding \in [Cars -> 0 .. LobbyPeople]
  /\ committed \in [Cars -> 0 .. LobbyPeople]
  /\ carUp \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ lobby \in 0 .. LobbyPeople

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ believes = [n \in Dispatchers |-> 0]
  /\ riding = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ committed = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ carUp = [c \in Cars |-> TRUE]
  /\ lobby = LobbyPeople

\* Failover: an election bumps the live term and leaves earlier leaders inert.
ElectLeader(n) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![n] = term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<riding, committed, carUp, lobby>>

\* A commitment is charged against both the car rating and the bank limit
\* the moment it is made, not when the passenger steps in.
CommitToCar(n, c) ==
  /\ LeadsNow(n)
  /\ lobby > 0
  /\ riding[c] + committed[c] < CarRating
  /\ InTransit < BankLimit
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![c] = committed[c] + 1]
  /\ lobby' = lobby - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, riding, carUp>>

StepIn(c) ==
  /\ carUp[c]
  /\ committed[c] > 0
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![c] = committed[c] - 1]
  /\ riding' = [riding EXCEPT ![c] = riding[c] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, carUp, lobby>>

Alight(c) ==
  /\ carUp[c]
  /\ riding[c] > 0
  /\ riding' = [riding EXCEPT ![c] = riding[c] - 1]
  /\ lobby' = lobby + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, committed, carUp>>

\* At most one controller fails, and it leaves no trace when it does.
CrashController(c) ==
  /\ \A d \in Cars : carUp[d]
  /\ carUp' = [carUp EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, riding, committed, lobby>>

HandWalkOut(c) ==
  /\ ~carUp[c]
  /\ riding[c] + committed[c] > 0
  /\ riding' = [riding EXCEPT ![c] = IF riding[c] > 0 THEN riding[c] - 1 ELSE 0]
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![c] =
        IF riding[c] > 0 THEN committed[c] ELSE committed[c] - 1]
  /\ lobby' = lobby + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, believes, carUp>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Dispatchers : ElectLeader(n)
  \/ \E n \in Dispatchers, c \in Cars : CommitToCar(n, c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : StepIn(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Alight(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : CrashController(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : HandWalkOut(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Two independent ceilings: each car's own rating, and the fire-code cap on
\* everybody in transit across the whole bank.
LoadWithinBothLimits ==
  /\ \A c \in Cars : riding[c] + committed[c] <= CarRating
  /\ SumOf(riding, NumCars) + SumOf(committed, NumCars) <= BankLimit
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumCars = 2
    Dispatchers = {n1, n2}
    CarRating = 2
    BankLimit = 3
    LobbyPeople = 3
    MaxTerm = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT LoadWithinBothLimits
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank is run by a cluster of dispatch computers, one of which is the elected leader. Leadership is carried by a term number: an election bumps the bank's term and installs the electing computer as leader of that term, and a computer may only dispatch while the term it believes it leads is the bank's live term. That is how the bank fails over when a dispatch computer drops out.

Two capacity limits govern the bank. Each car has a rated load: the people already riding in it plus the people the dispatcher has committed to it but who have not yet stepped in must never exceed that rating. On top of that the building fire code sets a bank-wide limit on how many people may be in transit at once, counting everyone riding and everyone committed to a car across the whole bank, and that limit is deliberately lower than the sum of the car ratings.

People wait in the lobby. The live leader may commit one waiting person to a car, but only if that car's riding-plus-committed count is still below its rating and the bank-wide in-transit count is still below the fire-code limit; committing takes the person out of the lobby. A person committed to a car with a working controller steps into the car, turning a commitment into a rider. A rider in a car with a working controller alights and returns to the lobby.

One car controller in the bank can crash silently: at most one controller ever fails, and it fails without telling anybody, so nothing in the dispatcher's records changes when it does. A crashed car simply stops loading and unloading, and its riders and commitments stay charged against both limits. A building engineer may hand-walk one person out of a crashed car, whether that person was riding or merely committed, and back to the lobby.

The full action set is: elect a dispatch computer as leader by bumping the bank's term, commit a waiting person to a car that has room under both its own rating and the bank-wide limit, step a committed person into a car with a working controller, alight a rider from a car with a working controller back to the lobby, crash the one car controller that is allowed to fail, and hand-walk one person out of a crashed car back to the lobby.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No car's riders plus commitments ever exceed that car's rated load, and the bank-wide count of riders plus commitments across all cars never exceeds the fire-code in-transit limit, even after a car controller has crashed silently and stopped clearing its load.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m6p6t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumAisles, GenCeiling, TimerFull

Aisles == 1 .. NumAisles
Robots == {"r1", "r2"}
Gens == 0 .. GenCeiling
NoRobot == "unleased"
NoAisle == 0
BlankTicket == [aisle |-> NoAisle, gen |-> 0]

VARIABLES holder, generation, timer, ticket, phase
vars == <<holder, generation, timer, ticket, phase>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ holder \in [Aisles -> Robots \cup {NoRobot}]
  /\ generation \in [Aisles -> Gens] /\ timer \in [Aisles -> 0 .. TimerFull]
  /\ ticket \in [Robots -> [aisle : Aisles \cup {NoAisle}, gen : Gens]]
  /\ phase \in [Robots -> {"idle", "moving"}]

Init ==
  /\ holder = [a \in Aisles |-> NoRobot]
  /\ generation = [a \in Aisles |-> 0] /\ timer = [a \in Aisles |-> 0]
  /\ ticket = [rb \in Robots |-> BlankTicket]
  /\ phase = [rb \in Robots |-> "idle"]

\* Every grant and every renewal bumps the generation, which is what makes
\* all older tickets for that aisle worthless.
GrantLease(a, rb) ==
  /\ holder[a] = NoRobot
  /\ generation[a] < GenCeiling
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![a] = rb]
  /\ generation' = [generation EXCEPT ![a] = generation[a] + 1]
  /\ timer' = [timer EXCEPT ![a] = TimerFull]
  /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![rb] = [aisle |-> a, gen |-> generation[a] + 1]]
  /\ UNCHANGED phase

RenewLease(a, rb) ==
  /\ holder[a] = rb
  /\ timer[a] > 0
  /\ generation[a] < GenCeiling
  /\ generation' = [generation EXCEPT ![a] = generation[a] + 1]
  /\ timer' = [timer EXCEPT ![a] = TimerFull]
  /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![rb] = [aisle |-> a, gen |-> generation[a] + 1]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, phase>>

StartMoving(rb) ==
  /\ phase[rb] = "idle"
  /\ ticket[rb].aisle # NoAisle /\ holder[ticket[rb].aisle] = rb
  /\ generation[ticket[rb].aisle] = ticket[rb].gen /\ timer[ticket[rb].aisle] > 0
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![rb] = "moving"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, generation, timer, ticket>>

\* Robots are slow but never fail: a job always ends.
FinishJob(rb) ==
  /\ phase[rb] = "moving"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![rb] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, generation, timer, ticket>>

RunDown(a) ==
  /\ timer[a] > 0
  /\ timer' = [timer EXCEPT ![a] = timer[a] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, generation, ticket, phase>>

\* A lease is never yanked out from under a robot that is mid-job.
TearDown(a) ==
  /\ holder[a] # NoRobot /\ timer[a] = 0
  /\ \A rb \in Robots : ~(phase[rb] = "moving" /\ ticket[rb].aisle = a)
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![a] = NoRobot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<generation, timer, ticket, phase>>

NewShift ==
  /\ (\A a \in Aisles : holder[a] = NoRobot) /\ (\A rb \in Robots : phase[rb] = "idle")
  /\ \E a \in Aisles : generation[a] = GenCeiling
  /\ generation' = [a \in Aisles |-> 0]
  /\ timer' = [a \in Aisles |-> 0]
  /\ ticket' = [rb \in Robots |-> BlankTicket]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, phase>>

FinishR1 == FinishJob("r1")
FinishR2 == FinishJob("r2")
TearDownAny == \E a \in Aisles : TearDown(a)

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Aisles, rb \in Robots : GrantLease(a, rb)
  \/ \E a \in Aisles, rb \in Robots : RenewLease(a, rb)
  \/ \E rb \in Robots : StartMoving(rb)
  \/ FinishR1 \/ FinishR2
  \/ \E a \in Aisles : RunDown(a)
  \/ TearDownAny
  \/ NewShift

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(FinishR1)
  /\ WF_vars(FinishR2)
  /\ WF_vars(TearDownAny)

\* A moving robot is on its own ticketed aisle, is that aisle's holder, and
\* its ticket generation still matches the aisle's live generation.
MovingIsTicketed ==
  \A rb \in Robots :
    phase[rb] = "moving" => /\ ticket[rb].aisle # NoAisle
                            /\ holder[ticket[rb].aisle] = rb
                            /\ generation[ticket[rb].aisle] = ticket[rb].gen

\* An expired lease is always eventually torn down.
ExpiredLeaseIsTornDown ==
  \A a \in Aisles : (timer[a] = 0 /\ holder[a] # NoRobot) ~> (holder[a] = NoRobot)
=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    NumAisles = 2
    GenCeiling = 2
    TimerFull = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT MovingIsTicketed

PROPERTY ExpiredLeaseIsTornDown
nl:
A warehouse floor is worked by a fleet of picking robots. Each aisle is handed out to one robot at a time under a lease, and a robot may only move stock in an aisle whose lease it genuinely holds right now. Leases are the whole authorisation story here: the warehouse controller does not track robot positions, so if a robot were to act on an aisle whose lease had moved on without it, nothing else would catch the mistake.

Every aisle carries a lease holder, a lease generation number and a run-down timer. Granting a free aisle's lease to a robot bumps that aisle's generation, refills the timer and hands the robot a ticket naming the aisle and the generation it was granted at. Renewing a live lease for the robot that already holds it bumps the generation again, refills the timer and reissues that robot's ticket. A ticket is therefore only good for the generation printed on it: the moment the aisle's generation moves on, every ticket printed under an earlier generation is stale and worthless. The generation counter runs only up to a fixed ceiling.

A robot may start moving stock in an aisle only if its ticket names that aisle, the aisle's lease holder is that same robot, the aisle's generation still matches the generation printed on the ticket, and the aisle's timer has not run out. The robots are slow but they never fail: a robot may take arbitrarily long over a job, but it always eventually finishes and goes idle. Aisle timers run down on their own. An aisle whose timer has run out has its lease torn down, but only once no robot is actually working in it, so a lease is never yanked out from under a robot mid-job; because robots always finish, the controller never has to wait for ever.

When every aisle is unleased, every robot is idle and some aisle's generation has reached the ceiling, the warehouse starts a new shift: generation counters go back to zero, timers are emptied and every robot's ticket is torn up together, so no ticket from the old shift can survive into the new one.

The full action set is: grant a free aisle's lease to a robot with a fresh generation and ticket, renew a live lease for its current holder with a new generation and ticket, start moving stock in an aisle against a matching, unexpired, live-generation ticket, finish a job and go idle, run an aisle's timer down by one, tear down an expired lease on an aisle nobody is working in, and start a new shift once everything is quiet and the generation ceiling has been reached.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any robot that is moving stock is working an aisle that its own ticket names, whose lease holder is that same robot, and whose lease generation still equals the generation printed on that ticket, so no unauthorised robot and no robot carrying a stale ticket ever moves stock.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Any aisle whose lease timer has run out while a lease is still held on it eventually has that lease torn down.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m5p0t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NorthPress, SouthPress, Arbiters, Jobs, Unpledged, Unplated, MisfeedCap

Presses == {NorthPress, SouthPress}

VARIABLES pressState, ballot, platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway
vars == <<pressState, ballot, platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

Pledged(p) == {a \in Arbiters : ballot[a] = p}
Uncommitted == {a \in Arbiters : ballot[a] = Unpledged}
HasQuorum(p) == 2 * Cardinality(Pledged(p)) > Cardinality(Arbiters)
QuorumHopeless(p) ==
  2 * (Cardinality(Pledged(p)) + Cardinality(Uncommitted)) <= Cardinality(Arbiters)

TypeOK ==
  /\ pressState \in [Presses -> {"idle", "canvassing", "mounted", "rebuffed"}]
  /\ ballot \in [Arbiters -> Presses \cup {Unpledged}]
  /\ platedBy \in [Jobs -> Presses \cup {Unplated}]
  /\ misfeeds \in 0 .. MisfeedCap
  /\ turnedAway \subseteq Presses

Init ==
  /\ pressState = [p \in Presses |-> "idle"]
  /\ ballot = [a \in Arbiters |-> Unpledged]
  /\ platedBy = [j \in Jobs |-> Unplated]
  /\ misfeeds = 0
  /\ turnedAway = {}

OpenCanvass(p) ==
  /\ pressState[p] = "idle"
  /\ pressState' = [pressState EXCEPT ![p] = "canvassing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

\* An arbiter pledges to at most one canvassing press, and defers to a branch
\* that was turned away last time so the same branch is not starved twice.
Pledge(a, p) ==
  /\ ballot[a] = Unpledged
  /\ pressState[p] = "canvassing"
  /\ ~ \E q \in Presses :
        /\ q # p
        /\ pressState[q] = "canvassing"
        /\ q \in turnedAway
        /\ p \notin turnedAway
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![a] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pressState, platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

\* A strict majority of arbiters is what puts a branch on the plate-setter.
Mount(p) ==
  /\ pressState[p] = "canvassing"
  /\ HasQuorum(p)
  /\ pressState' = [pressState EXCEPT ![p] = "mounted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

Rebuff(p) ==
  /\ pressState[p] = "canvassing"
  /\ QuorumHopeless(p)
  /\ pressState' = [pressState EXCEPT ![p] = "rebuffed"]
  /\ ballot' = [a \in Arbiters |-> IF ballot[a] = p THEN Unpledged ELSE ballot[a]]
  /\ turnedAway' = turnedAway \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<platedBy, misfeeds>>

PlateJob(p, j) ==
  /\ pressState[p] = "mounted"
  /\ platedBy[j] = Unplated
  /\ platedBy' = [platedBy EXCEPT ![j] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pressState, ballot, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

Misfeed ==
  /\ misfeeds < MisfeedCap
  /\ \E p \in Presses : pressState[p] = "mounted"
  /\ misfeeds' = misfeeds + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pressState, ballot, platedBy, turnedAway>>

StepDown(p) ==
  /\ pressState[p] \in {"mounted", "rebuffed"}
  /\ pressState' = [pressState EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
  /\ ballot' = [a \in Arbiters |-> IF ballot[a] = p THEN Unpledged ELSE ballot[a]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Presses : OpenCanvass(p)
  \/ \E a \in Arbiters, p \in Presses : Pledge(a, p)
  \/ \E p \in Presses : Mount(p)
  \/ \E p \in Presses : Rebuff(p)
  \/ \E p \in Presses, j \in Jobs : PlateJob(p, j)
  \/ Misfeed
  \/ \E p \in Presses : StepDown(p)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(\E a \in Arbiters : Pledge(a, NorthPress))
  /\ SF_vars(\E a \in Arbiters : Pledge(a, SouthPress))
  /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Presses : Mount(p))
  /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Presses : Rebuff(p))
  /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Presses : StepDown(p))

\* A branch is only on the plate-setter while it is holding a strict majority
\* of the arbiters, and two majorities of one arbiter pool always overlap.
MountedOnlyWithQuorum ==
  \A p \in Presses : pressState[p] = "mounted" => HasQuorum(p)

\* No canvass hangs: with an odd arbiter pool a branch either wins a majority
\* or provably cannot, and either way it is told so.
EveryCanvassEventuallyDecided ==
  \A p \in Presses :
    (pressState[p] = "canvassing") ~> (pressState[p] \in {"mounted", "rebuffed"})
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NorthPress = north
    SouthPress = south
    Arbiters = {v1, v2, v3}
    Jobs = {j1, j2}
    Unpledged = unpledged
    Unplated = unplated
    MisfeedCap = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT MountedOnlyWithQuorum

PROPERTY EveryCanvassEventuallyDecided
nl:
A print shop runs two independent press branches, north and south, which share one plate-setter and one pool of scheduling arbiters. Only one branch may be mounted on the plate-setter at a time, and the shop decides who gets it by quorum voting rather than by a single dispatcher.

An idle branch opens a canvass. Each arbiter may pledge itself to at most one canvassing branch, and an arbiter that is still unpledged will defer to a branch that was turned away in an earlier round, so the same branch is not starved twice in a row. A branch that has collected a strict majority of the arbiter pool mounts the plate-setter. A branch whose pledges plus the remaining unpledged arbiters could never add up to a majority is rebuffed instead: it gives back the pledges it had collected and is recorded as having been turned away.

While mounted, a branch plates jobs from the shop's shared job list, marking each plated job with the branch that did it. The plate-setter occasionally misfeeds while a branch is mounted, which the shop logs up to a small daily limit. A branch that is mounted or rebuffed eventually steps down back to idle, releasing any pledges still held in its name.

The full action set is: a branch opens a canvass, an arbiter pledges to a canvassing branch, a branch with a majority mounts the plate-setter, a branch with no path to a majority is rebuffed and returns its pledges, a mounted branch plates a job, the plate-setter misfeeds, and a mounted or rebuffed branch steps down and releases its pledges.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A branch is on the plate-setter only while it holds a strict majority of the arbiter pool, and since two majorities of one pool always share an arbiter, the two branches can never be mounted at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every canvass a branch opens is eventually decided, with the branch either mounting the plate-setter or being rebuffed.
